  let i = 0;
  while (i < text.length) {
    const c = text[i];
    const next = text[i + 1];

/**
 * check-no-secrets.ts — no secret and no personal datum in what would be published.
 *
 *   bun run tools/check-no-secrets.ts                 # tree + history + local store
 *   bun run tools/check-no-secrets.ts --no-local-store  # shape classes only (CI)
 *   bun run tools/check-no-secrets.ts --repo <dir> --rev <commit>   # one exact tree
 *   bun run tools/check-no-secrets.ts --dir <build output>          # every file, no git
 *
 * # Why this exists
 *
 * Phase 1 of `docs/PLAN-PUBLIC-LAUNCH-2026-09-22.md` makes this repository
 * public, and its gate is *"the secret sweep passing on the exact tree that will
 * be published"*. The plan says why it must be a gate and not a paragraph: **a
 * sweep recorded in prose is a claim with no falsifier** (`CLAIMS.md` E-137,
 * E-141). And this repository has shipped four gates that false-passed
 * (E-165, E-168, E-182, E-201), so this one runs its controls through the same
 * `scanRepo()` the real check calls, against a throwaway git repository it
 * builds with planted secrets, every time it runs.
 *
 * # What it looks for
 *
 * | class | what | allowed when |
 * |---|---|---|
 * | `seed` | an XRPL family seed in base58, either algorithm, checksum valid **or not** | its 16 bytes of entropy come from a published rule (`PUBLIC_ENTROPY`) |
 * | `seed-entropy-hex` | 32 hex digits after a `seed` or `entropy` label | same rule |
 * | `labelled-scalar` | 64 or 66 hex digits after a label with an `sk`, `secret` or `private` component | it is derived from public entropy, or is a cited test vector |
 * | `known-value` | **an exact value from the local secret store**, in every encoding listed in `needlesForSeed` | never |
 * | `credential` | PEM private keys and common API-token shapes | its variable part, after the pattern's fixed prefix, is one character repeated: a placeholder. A PEM header never |
 * | `secret-file` | a path named like a secret store (`state.json`, `profile.json`, `.env`, `*.pem`, ...) | never |
 * | `personal-path` | a home directory or a macOS per-user temp directory, in five encodings | the user name is generic (`runner`, `user`, ...) |
 * | `email` | an email address | reserved domains and three role addresses |
 *
 * **`known-value` is the only class that can see an UNLABELLED ElGamal secret.**
 * A bare 64-hex scalar is indistinguishable from a transaction hash, so no
 * shape rule can find one. That is why the default run REFUSES without the
 * local store: a run that skipped it would look like the phase 1 gate and not
 * be it. `--no-local-store` runs the shape classes and says so in its verdict
 * word (`PASS-SHAPES-ONLY`), so a CI log cannot be mistaken for the real gate.
 *
 * # What "published" means here
 *
 * * **The tree:** every file `git add -A` would commit — tracked plus
 *   untracked-not-ignored — read from disk. A gitignored file is not scanned,
 *   because it is not published; that is a property, and a control pins it.
 * * **`--rev`:** the blobs of exactly one commit's tree, read from git objects.
 *   ⚠ It scans no history. The publication is two commits, so the phase 1 gate
 *   is NOT this form: it is `--repo <export> --strict-history` on a clean export
 *   (`REVIEW-057` R1-7 and R2-7).
 * * **History:** every blob, commit message and tag message reachable from any
 *   ref, and every path any commit ever touched. ⚠ **Personal paths and emails
 *   in history are REPORTED, not failed**, because the launch plan rules that
 *   history is squashed at publication (`CLAIMS.md` E-309) and this repository
 *   stays the private archive. Secrets fail in history like anywhere else.
 *   `--strict-history` fails on both, and is the form for the export: its two
 *   commits are published history, so nothing in them may be merely reported.
 * * **`--dir`:** every regular file under one directory, read from disk with
 *   no git at all, dotfiles and gitignored files included. It is the form for a
 *   build output, which is uploaded whole: under the tree mode an ignored
 *   `dist/` file went unscanned (`REVIEW-058` R1-9). A symlink, a non-regular
 *   file and an archive it cannot open are refused. A whole file in gzip (found
 *   by its magic bytes) or brotli (by its `.br` name) is read decompressed as
 *   well as raw.
 *
 * **No path is exempt, including `docs/reviews/` and this file.** Exempting a
 * file is how a gate false-passes. This file contains no planted secret
 * literally: the controls generate theirs at runtime.
 *
 * # Exit codes and the verdict line
 *
 * `0` pass, `1` the scanned tree has findings, `2` a control failed or the gate
 * refused to run. **The last line of output is always
 * `check-no-secrets: verdict=<WORD> exit=<N>`**, and a caller must require it,
 * because Bun exits 1 on a crash too (`CLAIMS.md` E-259).
 *
 * # What it does NOT catch
 *
 * Printed every run by `printLimits()`, and each lexical limit is an
 * ASSERTED-UNCAUGHT control: if a later change starts catching one, the control
 * fails and the disclosure has to be updated rather than going stale
 * (E-203's shape, from `check-zeroize-bounds` part 6).
 */

import { createHash, randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import {
  existsSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readdirSync, readFileSync,
  readlinkSync, realpathSync, rmSync, symlinkSync, writeFileSync,
} from "node:fs";
import { homedir, tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { brotliCompressSync, brotliDecompressSync, gunzipSync, gzipSync } from "node:zlib";
import { encodeSeed } from "ripple-address-codec";
import { deriveKeypair } from "ripple-keypairs";
import { deriveElGamalKey } from "./wconf-keygen.ts";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- primitives

export const XRPL_ALPHABET = "rpshnaf39wBUDNEGHJKLM4PQRST7VWXYZ2bcdeCg65jkm8oFqi1tuvAxyz";
const B58 = new Map([...XRPL_ALPHABET].map((c, i) => [c, i] as const));

const sha256 = (b: Uint8Array) => new Uint8Array(createHash("sha256").update(b).digest());
function refuseTransformedTree(repo: string, paths: string[], gitlinks: string[], source?: string): void {
  if (gitlinks.length) throw new Error(`a submodule or nested repository at ${gitlinks.slice(0, 5).join(", ")}: its content is another repository and is not scanned`);
  if (!paths.length) return;
  // ⚠ For `--rev`, the attributes are read FROM THAT COMMIT with `--source`, and
  // parsed by git, so a comment that mentions `filter=` is not a filter (R2-6).
  const src = source ? ["--source", source] : [];
  const out = gitText(repo, ["check-attr", "-z", "--stdin", ...src, "filter", "working-tree-encoding"], paths.join("\0") + "\0").split("\0");
  const bad: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i + 2 < out.length; i += 3) if (out[i + 2] !== "unspecified" && out[i + 2] !== "unset") bad.push(`${out[i]} (${out[i + 1]}=${out[i + 2]})`);
  if (bad.length) throw new Error(`content-transforming attributes on ${bad.length} path(s), e.g. ${bad.slice(0, 3).join(", ")}: the published bytes are not the bytes on disk`);
}

/** What `git add -A` would commit, read from disk. Symlinks are not followed. */
export function treeUnits(repo: string): Unit[] {
  const names = gitText(repo, ["ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean);
  const staged = gitText(repo, ["ls-files", "-z", "-s"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean);
  const gitlinks = staged.filter((l) => l.startsWith("160000 ")).map((l) => l.slice(l.indexOf("\t") + 1));
  // An untracked nested repository is listed as a directory: `git add -A` would record a gitlink.
  gitlinks.push(...names.filter((n) => n.endsWith("/")));
  refuseTransformedTree(repo, names.filter((n) => !n.endsWith("/")), gitlinks);
  const units: Unit[] = [];
  for (const n of [...new Set(names)]) {
    const p = join(repo, n);
    units.push({ where: n, text: n, scope: "tree", kind: "path" });
    if (!existsSync(p) && !lstatSync(p, { throwIfNoEntry: false })) {
      // Deleted on disk, still in the index: the index copy is what a plain commit publishes.
      try { units.push({ where: n, text: asText(git(repo, ["cat-file", "blob", `:${n}`])), scope: "tree", kind: "file" }); } catch { /* not in index either */ }
      continue;
    }
    const s = lstatSync(p);
    if (s.isSymbolicLink()) units.push({ where: `${n} (symlink target)`, text: readlinkSync(p), scope: "tree", kind: "file" });
    else if (s.isFile()) units.push({ where: n, text: asText(readFileSync(p)), scope: "tree", kind: "file" });
  }
  return units;
}

/**
 * Magic bytes of archives this gate cannot open. A build output holding one is
 * refused rather than scanned as opaque bytes.
 */
const UNREADABLE_ARCHIVES: [string, number[]][] = [
  ["zip", [0x50, 0x4b, 0x03, 0x04]], ["zip", [0x50, 0x4b, 0x05, 0x06]],
  ["zstd", [0x28, 0xb5, 0x2f, 0xfd]], ["xz", [0xfd, 0x37, 0x7a, 0x58, 0x5a, 0x00]],
  ["7z", [0x37, 0x7a, 0xbc, 0xaf, 0x27, 0x1c]],
];
const DECOMPRESS_LIMIT = 256 * 1024 * 1024;
const startsWith = (b: Uint8Array, m: number[]) => b.length >= m.length && m.every((x, i) => b[i] === x);

/** The decompressed bytes of a whole-file gzip or brotli member, or null. */
function decompressed(path: string, body: Uint8Array): Uint8Array | null {
  for (const [name, magic] of UNREADABLE_ARCHIVES) if (startsWith(body, magic)) throw new Error(`${path} is a ${name} archive, which this gate cannot open`);
  let inner: Uint8Array | null = null;
  if (startsWith(body, [0x1f, 0x8b])) inner = gunzipSync(body, { maxOutputLength: DECOMPRESS_LIMIT });
  else if (/\.br$/i.test(path)) {
    try { inner = brotliDecompressSync(body, { maxOutputLength: DECOMPRESS_LIMIT }); }
    catch (e) { throw new Error(`${path} is named as brotli and does not decompress: ${String(e)}`); }
  }
  if (inner && (startsWith(inner, [0x1f, 0x8b]) || UNREADABLE_ARCHIVES.some(([, m]) => startsWith(inner!, m)))) {
    throw new Error(`${path} decompresses to another archive, which this gate does not open`);
  }
  return inner;
}

/**
 * Every regular file under `dir`, read from disk with no git filter. Paths are
 * relative to `dir`. ⚠ A decompressed copy is a second unit with `paths: 0`, so
 * the file count still counts files on disk.
 */
export function dirUnits(dir: string): Unit[] {
  const units: Unit[] = [];
  const walk = (rel: string) => {
    for (const name of readdirSync(join(dir, rel)).sort()) {
      const r = rel ? `${rel}/${name}` : name;
      const s = lstatSync(join(dir, r));
      if (s.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`a symlink at ${r}: an upload may follow it, and its target is not scanned`);
      units.push({ where: r, text: r, scope: "tree", kind: "path" });
      if (s.isDirectory()) { walk(r); continue; }
      if (!s.isFile()) throw new Error(`${r} is not a regular file`);
      const body = readFileSync(join(dir, r));
      units.push({ where: r, text: asText(body), scope: "tree", kind: "file" });
      const inner = decompressed(r, body);
      if (inner) units.push({ where: `${r} (decompressed)`, text: asText(inner), scope: "tree", kind: "file", paths: 0 });
    }
  };
  if (!lstatSync(dir).isDirectory()) throw new Error(`${dir} is not a directory`);
  walk("");
  return units;
}

/** Exactly the blobs of one commit's tree. */
export function revUnits(repo: string, rev: string): Unit[] {
  // ⚠ Split at the FIRST tab only: a path may itself contain one (REVIEW-056 S2-3).
  const entries = gitText(repo, ["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--full-tree", rev]).split("\0").filter(Boolean).map((l) => {
    const t = l.indexOf("\t");
    const [mode, type, sha] = l.slice(0, t).split(" ");
    return { mode, type, sha, path: l.slice(t + 1) };
  });
  const gitlinks = entries.filter((e) => e.type === "commit").map((e) => e.path);
  if (gitlinks.length) throw new Error(`a submodule at ${gitlinks.slice(0, 5).join(", ")}: its content is another repository and is not scanned`);
  const blobs = entries.filter((e) => e.type === "blob");
  refuseTransformedTree(repo, blobs.map((e) => e.path), [], rev);
    rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
  return { run: controlsRun, failed: controlsFailed };
}

const dummy = (cls: Cls): Finding => ({ cls, at: 0, shown: "x", why: "x", where: "x", line: 1, scope: "tree" });

// ------------------------------------------------------------- the decision

export interface ScanResult { findings: Finding[]; allowed: Map<string, number>; seenAllowed: Set<string>; unitsTree: number; unitsHistory: number }

export function scanRepo(repo: string, store: Store, o: { tree: boolean; history: boolean; rev?: string; dir?: string }): ScanResult {
  if (o.dir && (o.history || o.rev)) throw new Error("--dir scans one directory; it has no history and no revision");
  const t = o.tree ? (o.dir ? dirUnits(o.dir) : o.rev ? revUnits(repo, o.rev) : treeUnits(repo)) : [];
  const h = o.history ? historyUnits(repo) : [];
  const r = scanUnits([...t, ...h], store);
  // ⚠ Files are counted by PATH, not by unique blob (REVIEW-056 S5-3): two paths
  // with identical content are two published files.
  const files = (us: Unit[]) => us.filter((u) => u.kind === "file").reduce((n, u) => n + (u.paths ?? 1), 0);
  return { ...r, unitsTree: files(t), unitsHistory: h.filter((u) => u.kind !== "path").length };
}

interface DecideIn { findings: Finding[]; store: Store; requireStore: boolean; strictHistory: boolean; unitsTree: number; unitsHistory: number; tree: boolean; history: boolean }

export function decide(d: DecideIn): { exit: 0 | 1 | 2; word: string; failing: Finding[]; reported: Finding[]; why?: string } {
  if (d.requireStore && d.store.secrets === 0) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "no local secret store found; the known-value class cannot run (pass --no-local-store for the shape classes only)" };
  if (!d.tree && !d.history) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "nothing was selected to scan" };
  if ((d.tree && d.unitsTree === 0) || (d.history && d.unitsHistory === 0)) return { exit: 2, word: "REFUSED", failing: [], reported: [], why: "zero files scanned; an empty scan is not a pass" };
  const failing = d.findings.filter((f) => f.scope === "tree" || d.strictHistory || !PERSONAL.has(f.cls));
  const reported = d.findings.filter((f) => !failing.includes(f));
  if (failing.length) return { exit: 1, word: "FAIL", failing, reported };
  return { exit: 0, word: d.requireStore ? "PASS" : "PASS-SHAPES-ONLY", failing, reported };
}

function printLimits() {
  console.log("\nWhat this gate does NOT catch (each is an asserted-uncaught control):");
  for (const l of LIMITS) console.log(`  - ${l}`);
}

function printFindings(title: string, fs: Finding[], cap = 25) {
  if (!fs.length) return;
  console.log(`\n${title}: ${fs.length}`);
  const byCls = new Map<Cls, Finding[]>();
  for (const f of fs) byCls.set(f.cls, [...(byCls.get(f.cls) ?? []), f]);
  for (const [cls, list] of byCls) {
    const files = new Map<string, number>();
    for (const f of list) files.set(f.where, (files.get(f.where) ?? 0) + 1);
    console.log(`  ${cls}: ${list.length} in ${files.size} location(s)`);
    for (const f of list.slice(0, cap)) console.log(`    ${f.where}${f.line ? `:${f.line}` : ""}  ${f.why} — ${f.shown}`);
    if (list.length > cap) console.log(`    … ${list.length - cap} more; per location:`), [...files].slice(0, 60).forEach(([w, n]) => console.log(`      ${n}  ${w}`));
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------- main

/**
 * Parse the command line STRICTLY (`REVIEW-056` S5-1). An unknown flag, a
 * missing value or a contradictory pair is refused: a misspelled
 * `--strict-histroy` used to be ignored and the run reported a pass.
 */
export function parseArgs(argv: string[]): { flags: Set<string>; repo?: string; rev?: string; dir?: string; stores: string[] } {
  const FLAGS = new Set(["--no-local-store", "--history-only", "--tree-only", "--strict-history", "--controls-only"]);
  const OPTS = new Set(["--repo", "--rev", "--store", "--dir"]);
  const flags = new Set<string>();
  const out: { flags: Set<string>; repo?: string; rev?: string; dir?: string; stores: string[] } = { flags, stores: [] };
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
    const a = argv[i];
    if (FLAGS.has(a)) { flags.add(a); continue; }
    if (!OPTS.has(a)) throw new Error(`unknown argument '${a}'`);
    const v = argv[++i];
    if (v === undefined || v.startsWith("--")) throw new Error(`${a} needs a value`);
    if (a === "--store") out.stores.push(v);
    else if (a === "--repo") out.repo = v;
    else if (a === "--dir") out.dir = v;
    else out.rev = v;
  }
  if (out.dir && (out.repo || out.rev || flags.has("--history-only") || flags.has("--strict-history"))) {
    throw new Error("--dir scans one directory with no git; it cannot be combined with --repo, --rev, --history-only or --strict-history");
  }
  if (flags.has("--tree-only") && flags.has("--history-only")) throw new Error("--tree-only and --history-only together select nothing");
  if (out.rev && flags.has("--history-only")) throw new Error("--rev scans one tree; it cannot be combined with --history-only");
  if (flags.has("--strict-history") && (out.rev || flags.has("--tree-only"))) throw new Error("--strict-history has no effect without a history scan");
  if (flags.has("--no-local-store") && out.stores.length) throw new Error("--no-local-store and --store contradict each other");
  return out;
}

if (import.meta.main) {
  const finish = (word: string, exit: number): never => { console.log(`check-no-secrets: verdict=${word} exit=${exit}`); process.exit(exit); };
  // ⚠ Everything runs inside one try, so every failure ends with the verdict
  // line rather than a stack trace (`REVIEW-056` S5-2).
  try {
    const a = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
    const flag = (f: string) => a.flags.has(f);
    const repo = realpathSync(a.repo ?? join(import.meta.dir, ".."));
    const rev = a.rev;
    const dir = a.dir ? realpathSync(a.dir) : undefined;
    const requireStore = !flag("--no-local-store");
    const doTree = !flag("--history-only");
    const doHistory = !flag("--tree-only") && !rev && !dir;

    console.log(`check-no-secrets over ${dir ? `every file under ${dir}, with no git filter` : rev ? `the tree of ${rev}` : doTree ? "the publication set (what git add -A would commit)" : "nothing in the tree"}${doHistory ? " and all history" : ""}`);
    const c = runControls();
    console.log(`controls: ${c.run - c.failed.length}/${c.run} passed, run through the same scanRepo() as the real check`);
    if (c.failed.length) {
      for (const f of c.failed) console.log(`  CONTROL FAILED: ${f}`);
      console.log("The detector is wrong; nothing it would report can be believed.");
      finish("CONTROL-FAILED", 2);
    }
    // The fast self-check `break-no-secrets-gate.ts` drives: controls, and nothing else.
    if (flag("--controls-only")) finish("CONTROLS-PASS", 0);

    const store = requireStore ? loadStore(a.stores.length ? a.stores : defaultStorePaths()) : { files: [], needles: [], secrets: 0, publicSkipped: 0 };
    if (requireStore) console.log(`known-value: ${store.secrets} secret(s) from ${store.files.length} file(s) in the local store, ${store.needles.length} encodings searched; ${store.publicSkipped} stored seed(s) skipped as public by construction`);
    else console.log("known-value: NOT RUN (--no-local-store). An unlabelled ElGamal secret is invisible to this run. This is NOT the phase 1 gate.");

    const r = scanRepo(repo, store, { tree: doTree, history: doHistory, rev, dir });
    console.log(`scanned: ${r.unitsTree} file(s) in the tree, ${r.unitsHistory} history object(s)`);
    console.log("allowed (each rule, and how many hits it permitted):");
    for (const [k, n] of [...r.allowed].sort()) console.log(`  ${n}  ${k}`);

    if (doTree && !rev && !dir) {
      const stale = CITED_VECTORS.map((v) => v.source).filter((src) => !r.seenAllowed.has(src));
      if (stale.length) {
        for (const s of stale) console.log(`  STALE CITED VECTOR: ${s} — no longer present; remove it from CITED_VECTORS`);
        finish("CONTROL-FAILED", 2);
      }
    }

    const d = decide({ findings: r.findings, store, requireStore, strictHistory: flag("--strict-history"), unitsTree: r.unitsTree, unitsHistory: r.unitsHistory, tree: doTree, history: doHistory });
    if (d.why) console.log(`REFUSED: ${d.why}`);
    printFindings("FAILING", d.failing);
    printFindings("REPORTED, NOT FAILED (personal data in history; history is squashed at publication, CLAIMS.md E-309; --strict-history fails these)", d.reported, 5);
    printLimits();
    finish(d.word, d.exit);
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(`REFUSED: ${String(e)}`);
    finish("REFUSED", 2);
  }
}

> it is reset from time to time. Each value was read from Ripple's public Devnet
> endpoint, at the ledger and date shown, and a lying or lagging server behind it
> would have made it wrong. The page does not update: it shows Devnet as it was at
> that ledger, not as it is now. Nothing on this page signs or submits. Do not use a
> value shown here to build a transaction.*
>
> *Vercel, which hosts this page, sees your IP address and the pages you open.*

Under H1 the second paragraph gains: *"Your browser also connects to the public
Devnet node operated by Ripple, which sees your IP address and every account you
look up."*

⚠ Revision 1's wording said *"no amount can be published because of it"*, which is
true of the page and not of a reader who copies a displayed key into their own
tooling, where a lying node reaches F-23 through them. It named only Ripple as a
party that sees visitors, and Vercel sees every one. It omitted that Devnet has no
value and is reset (`REVIEW-058` B1-6, B1-7, S-4). ⚠ Revision 2's wording blamed any
difference from today's ledger on a lying or lagging server, when under H3 the page
is simply a fixed reading (B2-4). The public endpoint also keeps only recent
history, about a million ledgers on 2026-10-18 (E-319), so a visitor can check the
ledger shown against it for some weeks and not after.

| option | what it means |
|---|---|
| **Accept, by name, with this wording beside every ledger value** *(recommended)* | the same shape as E-151: the risk is unmet by name, and the page says so where the value is |
| Do not accept | no hosted demo with ledger values. ⚠ Revision 1 offered H3 here as the way to avoid the acceptance, and H3 reads one node too, at build time (`REVIEW-058` S-5) |

**Ruled 2026-10-19 by the owner: accepted, by name, with the wording above as
written.** The H1 sentence does not apply, because D-H1 was ruled H3.

Corroboration across independently operated Devnet nodes is not offered as an
option. Every Devnet host this repository names is under `rippletest.net`
(`git grep -ohiE` for `devnet` hostnames, 2026-10-19), so every endpoint it knows
has one operator. Whether an independently operated public Devnet node exists has
**not been searched** outside this repository. That is a named gap, not a
negative.

9. **The hosted demo — a static, read-only page on a public URL.** **SCOPED AND RULED 2026-10-19; BUILT AND GATED 2026-10-20, ~~NOT DEPLOYED~~ DEPLOYED THE SAME DAY. Its rotation ran three rounds and is closed (`REVIEW-058`).** `ADR-0004` is the decision record, `Accepted` at revision 5. It carries four decisions, D-H1 to D-H4, which the project owner ruled on 2026-10-19, each as recommended: H3, with an indefinite snapshot rebuilt by hand on an isolated build machine; the D-H2 wording accepted by name; A, no issuer figure; and the prebuilt CLI deploy (`CLAIMS.md` E-331). ⚠ **A public deployment fires two of step 8's own conditions**: its falsifier *"the API binds to anything but loopback"*, and `ADR-0003`'s trigger 5, egress. The hosted page is public by design, so step 8's loopback property does not carry over to it, and this step's falsifiers replace it.

   **What the step is, in one sentence, as D-H1 was ruled:** prerendered static pages, built from one pinned snapshot of public Devnet state with the reader the local tier already uses, each naming that ledger index and the date, with no code of this project running on a server per request and nothing sent by a visitor's browser except page loads to the host. ⚠ **This said the visitor's browser would read Devnet over WebSocket until `REVIEW-058` round one**, which found that reuse failing in a browser and pricing a second reader, and found that revision 1's claim that the gate could enumerate egress was false (`CLAIMS.md` E-328).

   **It is a second build target, not a replacement.** Step 8's local tier stays as it is. Its signer panel and `/api-doc` page are absent from the hosted build.

   **What this step may touch:** public Devnet ledger state, read at build time; and files built from a clean checkout of the public repository at a named commit, with its locked dependencies, named build variables only and no source maps, on a machine where `~/.wconf` and `/tmp/wconf` are not reachable. ⚠ Until revision 11 this also admitted browser reads under H1 and one issuer snapshot if D-H3 ruled it; the owner took neither (`CLAIMS.md` E-331).

   **What it may never touch:** any server-side request handler; any socket client or the signer's socket path; any secret, seed or private key, the demo issuer key included; any decryption routine in the shipped output; any input asking a visitor for a secret; any network but Devnet; any second ledger endpoint, as a fallback or otherwise; any analytics, toolbar or third-party script; and any account a visitor chooses, carried in a URL the host receives.

   **Its gate is a hosted part of `tools/check-web-readonly.ts`, run over the UPLOADED OUTPUT DIRECTORY and its routing configuration rather than the source**, verified by breaking it in both directions. `ADR-0004` lists what it must check. ⚠ It cannot check egress. ~~`check-no-secrets` has no directory mode yet, so the scan it relies on does not exist (`REVIEW-058` R1-9).~~ The directory mode exists since 2026-10-20 and the gate runs it (`CLAIMS.md` E-334).

   **Built 2026-10-20 (`CLAIMS.md` E-334).** `web/hosted/README.md` is the release procedure: an isolated container build from a commit, the gate (`check-web-readonly --hosted`), a headless-browser check under the output's own policy, a preflight, the owner's deploy and a comparison of what is served. ~~⚠ **Not deployed.** The gate fails on the current output until the owner rules on the email address in a bundled package's licence notice, and the deploy needs the owner's Vercel project and token.~~ ⚠ The owner ruled the email redacted (E-335), and this sentence stood until the deploy. **Deployed 2026-10-20** at `https://xrpl-confidential-positions.vercel.app`, from the public commit `34ed67a`, and what was served matched what the gate passed when compared that day (`CLAIMS.md` E-336).

   *Falsified if:* the shipped output contains a server function, an API route, a serverless function or middleware, in its files or its routing configuration; or contains a socket client, the signer socket path, a decryption routine or a secret-shaped value; or contains any file the provenance rule does not admit; or asks a visitor for a seed, a key or a secret; or permits a connection to anything but its named targets; or renders a ledger value without the risk wording, the network check and the ledger index it was read at; or renders a failed or negative read that cannot be placed in the pinned ledger as an empty account, or substitutes another source; or carries a visitor's lookup in a URL the host receives; or publishes an issuer figure, which D-H3 ruled out; or ships bytes or headers other than the ones the gate passed; or does not render the commit it was built from and the gate's verdict on it. *Also falsified if:* any of step 8's wording falsifiers holds on the hosted page.

## 7. What this architecture must never claim

/**
 * What every row shares, and what no key source changes.
 *
 * ⚠ **These are `CLAIMS.md` rows CITED, not restated.** A second copy of a
 * claim is a second thing to go stale, and this project has thirteen recorded
 * instances of exactly that.
 */
export const INVARIANTS = [
  { rule: "P-4", text: "No key source hides identities. The sender and receiver of every confidential transaction are public." },
  { rule: "P-9", text: "A holder is never private from the issuer. The issuer can always decrypt." },
  { rule: "P-10", text: "No key source supports rotation or recovery. XLS-96 supports neither." },
  { rule: "P-11", text: "No key source hides who transacts, when, or how often. Only amounts are hidden." },
  { rule: "F-1", text: "A newly created confidential balance is publicly identifiable as exactly zero." },
  { rule: "F-24", text: "Retiring a position in tranches publishes each tranche size." },
  { rule: "P-5", text: "None of this is secure, audited, non-custodial or production-ready, and the custody mode is a simulation." },
];
/**
 * The custody demo mode — architecture §6 step 8, decision D4.
 *
 * ⚠⚠ **THIS IS A SIMULATION AND EVERY VALUE IT RETURNS SAYS SO.** There is no
 * custody-platform integration behind it, no MPC and no HSM. It models a
 * **key-source shape** — a standalone ElGamal key plus an external signer — and
 * walks each flow to report which survive and which break, and why.
 *
 * ⚠ `CLAIMS.md` **P-5** forbids claiming more than is delivered, and
 * *"custody-compatible"* over a stub is exactly that kind of claim.
 * `disclosure.test.ts` fails if any surface stops saying this, and that test is
 * verified by breaking it.
 *
 * **What makes it more than a mock:** the verdicts are not hand-written per
 * flow. Each flow declares which *capabilities* it needs, and the verdict is
 * computed from what a custody-shaped key source actually has — so a flow added
 * later cannot be quietly marked "works".
 */

/** What a step of a flow requires. The only inputs a verdict is computed from. */
export type Requirement =
  | "xrpl-signature"        // the account key signs. A custody platform does this.
  | "elgamal-decrypt"       // read own confidential balance.
  | "elgamal-prove"         // produce the ZK proof over hidden values.
  | "policy-over-amount"    // an approval rule that reads the transferred value.
  | "policy-over-identity"  // an approval rule over destination, issuance or time.
  | "seed-material";        // the raw master seed must be available.

/**
 * What a **custody-shaped** key source has, and what it structurally cannot.
 *
 * ⚠ Derived from the two findings in `docs/research/CUSTODY-2026-08-28.md`, not
 * from a wish-list: seed material never leaves the platform (that is the
 * product), and an approval engine sees a proof rather than a value.
 */
export const CUSTODY_SHAPE: Record<Requirement, { available: boolean; because: string; caveat?: string }> = {
  "xrpl-signature": {
    available: true,
    because: "Signing is what a custody platform is for. The account key never leaves its boundary.",
  },
  "elgamal-decrypt": {
    available: true,
    because:
      "Only with a standalone ElGamal key, which moves the problem rather than solving it: something " +
      "outside the custody platform then holds a permanent decryption key for every balance this " +
      "account has held. Who that should be has had no review (CLAIMS.md E-117).",
    // ⚠ A flow that needs this survives only on that condition, so the walk
    // reports it on each flow. It was keyed on a "⚠" inside `because` until
    // 2026-10-20; the wording pass removed the marks, and a field cannot be
    // dropped by rewording a sentence.
    caveat: "Only with a standalone ElGamal key, held outside the custody platform (E-117).",
  },
  "elgamal-prove": {
    available: true,
    because: "The same standalone key. Proving needs the same secret decrypting does.",
  },
  "policy-over-amount": {
    available: false,
    because:
      "Structural: the transaction carries a proof, not a value, so a rule like 'two approvers above " +
      "$1M' has no amount to read. It is hidden from the policy engine too.",
  },
  "policy-over-identity": {
    available: true,
    because:
      "Destination, issuance and timing are public (CLAIMS.md P-4, P-11). Every policy over an " +
      "identity, a time or a count survives; every policy over a value does not.",
  },
  "seed-material": {
    available: false,
    because:
      "Structural: a custody platform never releases seed material, so a custodied account cannot " +
      "derive its own ElGamal key.",
  },
};

export interface Flow {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  requires: Requirement[];
}

export const FLOWS: Flow[] = [
  { id: "public-payment", label: "Send a public XRPL payment", requires: ["xrpl-signature"] },
  { id: "onboard-derived", label: "Onboard with the ruled derived key", requires: ["seed-material", "xrpl-signature"] },
  { id: "onboard-standalone", label: "Onboard with a standalone ElGamal key", requires: ["xrpl-signature", "elgamal-decrypt"] },
  { id: "read-own-balance", label: "Read own confidential balance", requires: ["elgamal-decrypt"] },
  { id: "confidential-send", label: "Send a confidential amount", requires: ["elgamal-decrypt", "elgamal-prove", "xrpl-signature"] },
  { id: "confidential-send-capped", label: "Send confidentially, under an amount-capped approval policy", requires: ["elgamal-decrypt", "elgamal-prove", "xrpl-signature", "policy-over-amount"] },
  { id: "confidential-send-allowlist", label: "Send confidentially, under a destination-allowlist policy", requires: ["elgamal-decrypt", "elgamal-prove", "xrpl-signature", "policy-over-identity"] },
  { id: "retire-tranches", label: "Retire a position in tranches", requires: ["elgamal-decrypt", "elgamal-prove", "xrpl-signature"] },
];

export interface FlowVerdict {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  survives: boolean;
  blockedBy: { requirement: Requirement; because: string }[];
  caveats: string[];
}

/** ⚠ Computed, never hand-written per flow. */
export function walkFlows(): { simulation: true; disclaimer: string; flows: FlowVerdict[] } {
  const flows = FLOWS.map((f) => {
    const blockedBy = f.requires
      .filter((r) => !CUSTODY_SHAPE[r].available)
      .map((r) => ({ requirement: r, because: CUSTODY_SHAPE[r].because }));
    const caveats = f.requires
      .filter((r) => CUSTODY_SHAPE[r].available && CUSTODY_SHAPE[r].caveat)
      .map((r) => CUSTODY_SHAPE[r].caveat!);
    if (f.id === "retire-tranches") {
      caveats.push(
        "Each tranche size and its timing is public: the amount is plaintext on every ConvertBack (CLAIMS.md F-24).",
      );
    }
    return { id: f.id, label: f.label, survives: blockedBy.length === 0, blockedBy, caveats };
  });

  return {
    simulation: true,
    disclaimer:
      "SIMULATION. No custody platform is integrated behind this: no MPC and no HSM. It models a " +
      "standalone ElGamal key plus an external signer, to show which flows survive and which break. " +
      "See docs/research/CUSTODY-2026-08-28.md.",
    flows,
  };
}

  The facility's ledger source is REMOTE and is trusted for amount
  confidentiality. CLAIMS.md F-23 is EXECUTED, not theoretical: a source that
  lies about a destination's HolderEncryptionKey makes the signer publish the
  amount encrypted under the liar's key, permanently, in public. TLS does not
  address it — it authenticates the channel to a node someone chose.

  B-15's step-7 answer was AMENDED by the project owner on 2026-08-25 to
  extend REVIEW-019's named risk acceptance to this demo. That amendment, like
  the ruling it amends, has had NO adversarial review.

  What a run under this hatch CAN establish: that the transactions serialise,
  that rippled accepts them, that the balances decrypt to what the book
  predicts, and what a full-ledger observer sees.

  ⚠ It does NOT establish XLS-0096 §10.5's state changes. This sentence said it
  did, while run-facility.ts's own header said it did not — REVIEW-023 found the
  pair. The driver checks the outstanding-amount delta on the float conversion
  and reconciles decrypted balances; there are no per-movement assertions over
  the public amount or the balance version. CLAIMS.md B-18.

  What it CANNOT establish: anything whatever about the loopback obligation.
  Do not record a run under this hatch as evidence that the facility keeps it.

from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path
class Text(HTMLParser):
 def __init__(self): super().__init__();self.ignore=0;self.result=[]
 def handle_starttag(self,t,a):
  if t in ('script','style'):self.ignore+=1
  elif t in ('p','div','h1','h2','h3','li','tr','footer'):self.result.append('\\n')
 def handle_endtag(self,t):
  if t in ('script','style'):self.ignore-=1
 def handle_data(self,d):
  if not self.ignore:self.result.append(d)
for p in sorted(Path('review-input/deployed/.vercel/output/static').rglob('*.html')):
 print('\\nFILE',p)
 t=Text();t.feed(p.read_text());print('\\n'.join(' '.join(s.split()) for s in ''.join(t.result).split('\\n') if s.strip()))

W-CONF: confidential MPT on the XRPL Devnet
Devnet snapshot · signs nothing, holds no keys · not secure, not audited, not production-ready (P-5)
W-CONF
What confidential MPT on the XRP Ledger hides, and what it does not. A research project, shown on one snapshot of the Devnet.OverviewCapability matrixObserver viewIssuer viewWalletCustody
Capability matrix
What each key source can and cannot do. The ElGamal key encrypts and decrypts confidential balances; the XRPL account key signs. The rows follow the signer’s ownKeySource type, which has two variants, and rows that are not built say so.
key sourcedecrypt own balanceprove + sign confidentialpublic transactionsexists today
Generated demo seed, faucet-funded
derived-from-master-seedyes
The ElGamal secret is derived from the master seed, so the signer rebuilds it from the seed alone.
docs/reviews/REVIEW-012-RULING-keygen-2026-08-18.md; signer/src/keygen.rsyes
One seed gives both the ElGamal secret and the XRPL account key.
signer/src/keygen.rs; signer/src/onboarding.rsyes
An ordinary XRPL account. Public transactions are unaffected.
signer/src/xrpl.rsbuilt
signer/src/onboarding.rs
Existing Devnet seed, pasted
derived-from-master-seedyes
Same as a generated seed: the derivation does not depend on where the seed came from.
signer/src/keygen.rsconditional
Only if the master key controls the account. With a regular key or a signer list, spending authority may sit elsewhere, so the signer warns; with lsfDisableMaster it refuses.
signer/src/session.rs (REFUSED_MASTER_KEY_DISABLED); issue #11; REVIEW-012 condition 2yes
An ordinary XRPL account.
signer/src/xrpl.rsbuilt
signer/src/onboarding.rs
Standalone ElGamal key
standaloneyes
A separate ElGamal secret kept in the profile: two secrets to keep instead of one.
signer/src/onboarding.rs:279; signer/src/holder.rs:48conditional
The ElGamal key decrypts and proves but does not sign; the account key is a separate secret. A custody platform ends up here, and who then holds the ElGamal key is an open question (E-117).
CLAIMS.md E-117; signer/src/holder.rsyes
Unaffected: the ElGamal key plays no part in public transactions.
signer/src/xrpl.rsbuilt
signer/src/holder.rs — KeySource::Standalone
Browser wallet extensionno
Decrypting needs the ElGamal secret, which is derived from the master seed, and a wallet exists to keep the seed in. None of the three wallets examined on 2026-08-28 (Xaman, GemWallet, Crossmark) decrypts for a page or gives it a key. A wallet that derived the key and decrypted internally could; none examined does (E-329).
REVIEW-012 (derivation from master seed); ADR-0003 D2no
A confidential transaction needs the ElGamal secret and the account key. These wallets supply only the account key, so a page cannot assemble the transaction through them. A wallet that held the ElGamal key and built the proofs itself could; none examined does (E-329).
ADR-0003 D2; signer/src/keygen.rsyes
Ordinary transactions are what a wallet is for. Per each vendor's docs on 2026-08-28, the GemWallet, Crossmark and Xaman APIs accept any transaction type to sign and submit.
gemwallet.app API reference; docs.crossmark.io; docs.xaman.dev (all read 2026-08-28)not built
not built, for the reasons in this row
Custody platform (simulated)
standaloneconditional
Only with a standalone ElGamal key, held by something other than the custody platform. A custodied account cannot derive its own key, because that needs the seed, and a custody platform never releases the seed.
REVIEW-012; CLAIMS.md E-117conditional
The external signer can sign. It cannot apply a policy to the amount, because the transaction carries a proof, not a value: a rule like 'two approvers above $1M' has nothing to read.
docs/research/CUSTODY-2026-08-28.md; CLAIMS.md P-4yes
Public transactions carry plain amounts, so approval policies work as usual.
docs/research/CUSTODY-2026-08-28.mdnot built
Simulation: an external-signer stub. No MPC, no HSM, no integration.
Shown before the seed is asked for
The master seed becomes a permanent decryption credential. Anyone who ever holds it can decrypt every confidential balance this account has held, past and future. XLS-96 has no key rotation and no key recovery (P-10), so this cannot be undone.
The derivation is specified only in this repository and is not a published standard. A holder with their seed but without this repository cannot reconstruct their key. Issue #10 tracks this.
Required by the key-derivation ruling, REVIEW-012 condition 2.
What no key source changes
P-4No key source hides identities. The sender and receiver of every confidential transaction are public.
P-9A holder is never private from the issuer. The issuer can always decrypt.
P-10No key source supports rotation or recovery. XLS-96 supports neither.
P-11No key source hides who transacts, when, or how often. Only amounts are hidden.
F-1A newly created confidential balance is publicly identifiable as exactly zero.
F-24Retiring a position in tranches publishes each tranche size.
P-5None of this is secure, audited, non-custodial or production-ready, and the custody mode is a simulation.
Built from commit ccf76e73bf66 of the public repository. Ledger values were read at validated ledger 6263910 on 2026-10-20T05:22:05.191Z.
This page is published at https://xrpl-confidential-positions.vercel.app. A copy hosted anywhere else is not this build.
Gate verdict: not loaded (it is read from /gate-verdict.json once the page's script runs) (gate-verdict.json)

FILE review-input/deployed/.vercel/output/static/custody/index.html
W-CONF: confidential MPT on the XRPL Devnet
Devnet snapshot · signs nothing, holds no keys · not secure, not audited, not production-ready (P-5)
W-CONF
What confidential MPT on the XRP Ledger hides, and what it does not. A research project, shown on one snapshot of the Devnet.OverviewCapability matrixObserver viewIssuer viewWalletCustody
This is a simulation
No custody platform is integrated behind this page: no MPC, no HSM, no Harmonize. It models a key-source shape, a standalone ElGamal key plus an external signer, to show which flows survive and which break.
Two findings
1. The derived key does not work with custodial key management
The ElGamal secret is derived from the master seed, and a custody platform never releases the seed. So a custodied account cannot derive its own ElGamal key or read its own confidential balance.
A standalone ElGamal key gets around this, but then something outside the custody platform holds a permanent decryption key. Who that should be is an open question in this project (CLAIMS.md E-117).
2. Approval policies cannot read a confidential amount
An approval workflow sees a proof, not a value, so a rule like “two approvers above $1M” has nothing to check. This is structural, not an integration detail: confidentiality and amount-based approval policies pull against each other.
Which flows survive, and which break
Each flow lists what it needs, and the verdict is computed from what a custody-shaped key source has.
Note 1: Only with a standalone ElGamal key, held outside the custody platform (E-117).
survives: Send a public XRPL payment
breaks: Onboard with the ruled derived key
Structural: a custody platform never releases seed material, so a custodied account cannot derive its own ElGamal key.
survives: Onboard with a standalone ElGamal key (note 1)
survives: Read own confidential balance (note 1)
survives: Send a confidential amount (note 1)
breaks: Send confidentially, under an amount-capped approval policy (note 1)
Structural: the transaction carries a proof, not a value, so a rule like 'two approvers above $1M' has no amount to read. It is hidden from the policy engine too.
survives: Send confidentially, under a destination-allowlist policy (note 1)
survives: Retire a position in tranches (note 1)
Each tranche size and its timing is public: the amount is plaintext on every ConvertBack (CLAIMS.md F-24).

W-CONF: confidential MPT on the XRPL Devnet
Devnet snapshot · signs nothing, holds no keys · not secure, not audited, not production-ready (P-5)
W-CONF
What confidential MPT on the XRP Ledger hides, and what it does not. A research project, shown on one snapshot of the Devnet.OverviewCapability matrixObserver viewIssuer viewWalletCustody
What this is
A read-only look at confidential MPT positions on the XRPL Devnet. Every value comes from one snapshot of the ledger, taken when this site was built. The site signs nothing and holds no keys. No code of this project runs on a server when you load it, and your browser requests only this site’s own files.
Start here
Capability matrix: what each kind of key can and cannot do.
Observer view: what anyone can read on the ledger, including which balances are visibly zero.
Issuer view: the issuer’s copy of each balance, without the figure.
Wallet: why the browser wallets examined cannot hold a confidential position.
Custody: where confidentiality and custody approval policies conflict.
To transact, run it yourself
Signing happens only in wconf-signer, a separate program on the holder’s own machine, never in a web page. The README explains how to build it and run the local version of this site. It does not yet explain how to create a holder profile and funded Devnet accounts, which a transaction needs.
README, “Run it”
What it never claims
P-4No key source hides identities. The sender and receiver of every confidential transaction are public.
P-9A holder is never private from the issuer. The issuer can always decrypt.
P-10No key source supports rotation or recovery. XLS-96 supports neither.
P-11No key source hides who transacts, when, or how often. Only amounts are hidden.
F-1A newly created confidential balance is publicly identifiable as exactly zero.
F-24Retiring a position in tranches publishes each tranche size.
P-5None of this is secure, audited, non-custodial or production-ready, and the custody mode is a simulation.
Each label is a row in the repository’s CLAIMS.md.

A holder is never private from the issuer
The protocol keeps a second copy of every confidential balance, the IssuerEncryptedBalance, encrypted to the issuer’s key. The issuer can always decrypt it, and no setting turns this off (CLAIMS.md P-9).
This page shows that each copy is on the ledger. It does not show the decrypted figures: a visitor could not check them, so this project does not publish them (ADR-0004 D-H3).

FILE review-input/deployed/.vercel/output/static/wallet/index.html
W-CONF: confidential MPT on the XRPL Devnet
Devnet snapshot · signs nothing, holds no keys · not secure, not audited, not production-ready (P-5)
W-CONF
What confidential MPT on the XRP Ledger hides, and what it does not. A research project, shown on one snapshot of the Devnet.OverviewCapability matrixObserver viewIssuer viewWalletCustody
A browser wallet cannot hold a confidential position
The three wallets examined (Xaman, GemWallet and Crossmark, on 2026-08-28) cannot, and the reasons are structural, not missing features. A wallet that kept the ElGamal key inside the extension and offered a prove-and-sign operation could; none of those examined does.
A confidential transaction needs two secrets: the ElGamal secret, to decrypt the balance and build the proof, and the XRPL account key, to sign. A wallet supplies only the second.
Under the ruled key generation, the ElGamal secret is derived from the master seed. A derived-key account has no other way to get it.
A wallet extension exists in order not to release seed material. That is the product, not a gap in its API.
So a page cannot assemble the transaction through these wallets. They are not refusing a permission; they hold nothing they are built to give a page.
What a wallet can do
yes
Ordinary XRPL transactions
Ordinary transactions are what a wallet is for. Per each vendor's docs on 2026-08-28, the GemWallet, Crossmark and Xaman APIs accept any transaction type to sign and submit.
gemwallet.app API reference; docs.crossmark.io; docs.xaman.dev (all read 2026-08-28)
yes
Prove control of an account
Enough to show that account’s observer view, which anyone with the address can read anyway.
What this page does not claim
Not determined: whether a given wallet build can serialise XLS-0096 transactions. The page-side SDKs carry no codec, so serialisation happens inside the extension, whose version no vendor publishes. This is not why a wallet cannot hold a confidential position: the reasons above are structural, and this one could change with any release.
CLAIMS.md E-206.

168:| E-117 | ⚠ **Rejecting the XLS-65 `Vault` traded away a custody property, and ~~ADR-0002 does not say so~~ ADR-0002 has said so since `c34dcec` (E-256, E-295).** A `Vault`'s pseudo-account holds pooled assets **with no key** — nothing can move them outside the protocol's rules. The Dedicated Account that replaces it is an **ordinary XRPL account with an ordinary key**, so whoever holds that key can move the entire float. Rev 4 rejected the hybrid on blocker 1 (share tokens cannot be confidential) and that reasoning stands. ⚠ ~~*the comparison table counts only disclosure and accounting; it has no row for custody*~~ **— STRUCK 2026-09-09, and it was false from the commit that wrote this row.** `c34dcec` added **both** E-117 and the `Custody of the pooled float` row it says is missing, so the clause described a state its own commit had already ended and then read as live for twenty days. The real axis is sharper than the ADR states it: **confidential positions, or non-custodial pooling — one or the other, today.** This project picks confidentiality because that is its premise, and a design needing *"no single party can move the float"* would weigh it the other way | **Noticed 2026-08-20** while answering where a `Vault` *would* fit, which is a question the ADR never asks. ⚠ **Not a reversal of rev 4** — it is a cost rev 4 does not price. ⚠ **Both premises verified 2026-09-09, and the first is STRONGER than this row states it.** rippled 3.3.0 `src/libxrpl/ledger/helpers/AccountRootHelpers.cpp:565-604`, `createPseudoAccount`: `sfFlags` is set to `lsfDisableMaster \| lsfDefaultRipple \| lsfDepositAuth` at `:597`, and `sfSequence` to **0** under `featureSingleAssetVault` at `:588-593`, over the comment *"Pseudo-accounts can't submit transactions … an extra level of protection"*. So it is not merely that nobody holds a key: the master is disabled, deposit authorisation is on, and the sequence number cannot support a transaction. 266:| E-206 | ⚠⚠ **D2's FOURTH REASON — *"the extension's codec does not know the XLS-0096 types, so it could not serialise a `ConfidentialMPTSend`"* — IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS ALSO NOT NEEDED.** Checked at the wallets' own published sources, **2026-08-28**: (1) **GemWallet's API reference lists raw-transaction methods** — `signTransaction`, `submitTransaction`, `submitBulkTransactions` — documented as taking *"transaction payloads as defined in the XRPL Protocol"*. (2) **Crossmark documents `sign`, `submit`, `signAndSubmit`, `bulkSign`, `bulkSubmit` and the `…AndWait` forms**, over arbitrary transaction objects. (3) **Xaman's payload API accepts `txjson` *and* `txblob`**, a pre-serialised HEX blob. ⚠ **So all three accept an arbitrary `TransactionType` at the API surface, and the premise that a wallet cannot express one of these transactions is wrong at that layer.** ⚠⚠ **AND THE CODEC VERSION IS NOT KNOWABLE FROM ANY PUBLISHED SOURCE:** `npm view` on all three page-side packages, 2026-08-28 — `@crossmarkio/sdk@0.4.0` depends on `events` and `@crossmarkio/typings` **only**; `@gemwallet/api@3.8.0` and `xumm@1.8.0` are likewise bridges — **none carries `ripple-binary-codec` or `xrpl.js` at all.** Serialisation happens **inside the closed extension bundle**, or in Xaman's backend, and no wallet publishes that version. ⚠ **Xaman's docs additionally say it *"can add missing fields (signer account, fee, sequence)"*, which implies it PARSES even on the `txblob` path — so the blob route is not a clean bypass either, and that too is undetermined.** ⚠⚠ **The reason this matters is not that the claim is false — it is that it was the WRONG ARGUMENT TO LEAD WITH.** It is a **version fact an upstream release can close at any time**, whereas D2's reasons 1–3 are **structural**: a confidential operation needs the ElGamal secret AND the account key; the ElGamal secret is derived from the master seed under `REVIEW-012`; and a wallet extension exists in order not to release seed material. **A demonstration built on reason 4 would be falsified by a wallet update; one built on reasons 1–3 cannot be.** ⚠ **This is `CLAUDE.md`'s own P-12 shape** — an assertion about what a corpus does not contain, carried as a premise without the search that would settle it | **Reason 4 is WITHDRAWN as a premise and recorded as a NAMED GAP**, in `web/api/capability.ts` (the browser-wallet row's `publicTransactions` cell is `unverified` and says why), in the wallet route's own copy, and in `ADR-0003` D2. ⚠ **Nothing was backfilled from secondary coverage**: the Crossmark method list came from `docs.crossmark.io` directly, and the one search-summary source was re-fetched at the vendor's own site before use. **The demonstration now rests on reasons 1–3 only**, which is both honest and stronger. **Determining a given wallet build's codec would need testing against a live extension, which this repository cannot do reproducibly** — so it stays a gap rather than becoming an assumption | A, measured |
271:| E-211 | ⚠⚠ **A FALSE DISCLOSURE SENTENCE SHIPPED ON THE OBSERVER PAGE, AND IT IS F-24's SHAPE A THIRD TIME.** For any ciphertext not matching the canonical `EncZero`, the page said *"**Non-zero**, and the amount is hidden from an observer."* **That is false.** Measured on Devnet 2026-08-28: holder `rDYMkRMh7o7QfkNaoGvtd7TgFzmt12FEM8` decrypts to **0** through the issuer mirror, while its `ConfidentialBalanceSpending` does **not** match the canonical `EncZero` recomputed from its own registered key. ⚠⚠ **A BALANCE CAN BE EXACTLY ZERO AND NOT PUBLICLY IDENTIFIABLE AS ZERO.** F-1's canonical form is used on **first-time init, merge reset and clawback**; a balance that reached zero **by spending** is a homomorphic result — a randomised encryption of zero that matches nothing and looks identical to any other hidden value. ⚠⚠ **`tools/observer-harness.ts:277` HAD IT RIGHT AND THE WEB TIER FLATTENED THE HEDGE**: *"not the canonical zero (some non-zero value, or never reset)"* became *"Non-zero"*. **The correct source was one import away, in a file this module already imports `canonicalEncZero` from.** ⚠ **The wording tests did not catch it because it is a SEMANTIC error, not a phrasing one** — every guard was about privacy claims, and this is a claim about arithmetic. ⚠⚠ **AND THE PROTOCOL FACT WAS ALREADY IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN UPSTREAM REGISTER**: `UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md` **U-47** — *"a confidential balance that has been emptied by `ConvertBack` is not the canonical `EncZero`"* — observed on Devnet and written up before this tier existed. **So this is not a fact the project had to discover; it is one it had recorded, filed under its own heading, and then contradicted on a screen.** That is E-141's shape at the level of a whole register rather than a count | **Corrected 2026-08-28.** The note now states that a non-match means the value cannot be determined, that this is **not** the same as non-zero, and that a spent-to-zero balance looks exactly the same; F-1's line in *what is public* carries its condition; and the *what is hidden* entry no longer describes the hidden value as non-zero. ⚠ **The notes and both lists are now exported CONSTANTS and the tests assert on VALUES, not source text** — the first version scanned the file and failed on the **comment documenting this very bug**, which is E-182's shape inside a test. **Verified by breaking it**: reverting to the exact shipped sentence fails the suite, as does dropping F-1's condition | A, measured |
301:| E-241 | ⚠⚠ **THE ISSUER ROUTE IS RULED AND THE DISCLOSURE IS REMOVED RATHER THAN GUARDED — OPTION 2, 2026-09-05.** `GET /api/issuer/:account/:issuanceId` no longer returns `decrypted`; it reports **`decryptable`** — *whether* the issuer could read the balance — and never the figure. `GET /api/signer` no longer returns `socketPath` or the signer's `note`, which carried the holder address, the randomness-ledger generation id and its **entry count** — and `signer/src/store.rs:753-756` commits a record for *"a cancelled confirmation, a failed proof, an aborted attempt"*, so that count includes work **no observer can reconstruct**. ⚠ **This is E-212's own remedy applied one layer further**: that fix moved the KEY out and left the RESULT leaving. **There is now no request that reaches a decryption and none that returns one, so there is still nothing to authenticate.** ⚠ **What the demonstration keeps is the point it was making** — that the issuer can read any balance is proved by `IssuerEncryptedBalance` being populated on the ledger (P-9). **The plaintext integer only ever demonstrated that THIS PROJECT holds the demo issuer key**, and it lives in `tools/issuer-decrypt-balance.ts`, which is where `CLAUDE.md` says the issuer view belongs | **Falsifier: `disclosure.test.ts` — *"the decrypted balance is NEVER served, even when the snapshot has it"*, which asserts the figure appears NOWHERE in the serialised response while the public `MPTAmount` still does.** ⚠ **Verified by reverting the withholding: that test fails and it is the ONLY one that does** — a test that passes against the reverted code proves nothing. A second control asserts the withholding is not vacuous, distinguishing an absent value from a withheld one. **129 web tests, both type-checks clean.** ⚠⚠ **THIS DOES NOT MAKE THE TIER uid-SAFE; IT MAKES IT DISCLOSE NOTHING WORTH uid-PROTECTING.** `ADR-0003` trigger 5 (EGRESS) stays in the falsifier list, because the next route someone adds is where it fires again. **E-228 is closed by removal.** `ADR-0003`'s last open acceptance precondition is discharged | A, measured |
449:| F-1 | Docs claim the reset inbox value is indistinguishable; it is the canonical `EncZero`, recomputable by any observer from public inputs, and used on first-time init, merge reset and clawback | `ConfidentialMPTConvert.cpp:305–313`, `MergeInbox.cpp:111–114`, `Clawback.cpp:138–166`. **Executed on Devnet 2026-08-17 → E-49**: recomputed independently and byte-matched against a live `sfConfidentialBalanceSpending`. No longer a source reading | A |
<div align="center">

# W-CONF

### A Confidential MPT reference application for the XRP Ledger.

*Built to find out what XLS-96 actually hides — by execution, not by reading.*

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-3b82f6)](LICENSE)
[![Network](https://img.shields.io/badge/network-Devnet%20only-e11d48)](#amendment-status)
[![Spec](https://img.shields.io/badge/XLS--0096-Final-22c55e)](https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/tree/master/XLS-0096-confidential-mpt)
[![Signer](https://img.shields.io/badge/signer-Rust-000000?logo=rust&logoColor=white)](signer/)
[![Runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-Bun-000000?logo=bun&logoColor=white)](https://bun.sh)
[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-research%20artifact-6366f1)](#what-is-open)

[**What it hides**](#what-xls-96-hides-and-what-it-does-not) · [**Run it**](#run-it) · [**Findings**](docs/explainer/PROTOCOL-FINDINGS-2026-09-02.md) · [**What is open**](#what-is-open) · [**Claims register**](CLAIMS.md)

</div>

---

> **Public history starts at publication.** This repository was developed privately from 2026-08-16 and published on 2026-10-19 as two commits: the tree, and its revision log regenerated from this history. The commit hashes cited in `CLAIMS.md` and `docs/reviews/` refer to that private archive and do not resolve here. Issues #1 to #13 were copied from the archive in order, so the issue numbers cited here resolve; the ten closed ones are stubs.

**A confidential receivables facility on the XRP Ledger.** A bank opens a facility; suppliers enrol, draw down against invoices and repay; the facility retires in tranches. Every position is an encrypted balance on a public ledger. It has run on Devnet, and the point of building it was to establish exactly what an outside observer sees while it does.

**The short answer: XLS-96 hides balances and the amounts of confidential transfers, and nothing else, and even a balance is recognisable when it holds the canonical encrypted zero.** Converting into or out of confidential form publishes the amount in plaintext. Who pays whom, when and how often is public. The issuer can decrypt every balance. The details, with evidence, are [below](#what-xls-96-hides-and-what-it-does-not).

> ⚠ **Devnet only. No mainnet writes, at any phase.** This repository has not been audited, is not production-ready, and is not safe to put value behind.

It exercises Multi-Purpose Tokens (XLS-33) and Confidential Transfers (XLS-96, specified in the document XLS-0096, `Final` since 2026-09-03, read on 2026-10-18: E-1) together. It does not use Credentials (XLS-70) or Permissioned Domains (XLS-80).

> **Citations.** Ids such as *(E-58)* point to rows of [`CLAIMS.md`](CLAIMS.md), the register that governs what this project may claim: **E** is established evidence, **F** a finding, **P** a standing prohibition, **B** a blocker, open or ruled, and **R** a correction to something this project claimed earlier. Where this README and a row disagree, the row wins. Bare issue numbers are issues on this repository.

<details>
<summary><b>Terms, if you are new to XLS-96 or the XRPL</b></summary>

| term | meaning here |
|---|---|
| **MPT** | Multi-Purpose Token (XLS-33). `MPTokenIssuance` defines a token; an `MPToken` is one holder's position in it. |
| **Confidential balance** | A balance held as an ElGamal ciphertext on the ledger. Each holder has two: a *spending* balance and an *inbox* that receives transfers, folded in by `ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox`. |
| **`sk_A`** | A holder's ElGamal secret key. It decrypts that holder's balance and is needed to prove a `ConfidentialMPTSend`. |
| **Convert / Send / ConvertBack** | `ConfidentialMPTConvert` moves plaintext into confidential form, `ConfidentialMPTSend` moves a hidden amount between holders, `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack` moves it back out. Only Send hides its amount. |
| **Encrypted zero (`EncZero`)** | The canonical ciphertext of zero, which anyone can recompute. It is written on first initialisation, merge reset and clawback only. |
| **Proofs** | `Send` carries a 192-byte compact sigma proof and a 754-byte aggregated Bulletproof; `ConvertBack` a 128-byte sigma and a 688-byte Bulletproof; `Convert` and `Clawback` a 64-byte proof each; `MergeInbox` none. |
| **`tec` codes** | A `tec` result is *applied to the ledger*: it consumes a sequence number and its fields persist, ciphertexts included. |
| **`fail_hard`** | The submission parameter that asks a node to discard a failing transaction instead of applying it. Internal documents here use `tapFailHard` as shorthand for it; see [`docs/VOCABULARY.md`](docs/VOCABULARY.md). |
| **Dedicated Account** | The facility's own holding account. It is not an XLS-65 `Vault`, which cannot hold confidential balances. |
| **UDS** | Unix domain socket, a local channel no browser API can open. |
| **Loopback** | A node or service on the same machine, reached at `127.0.0.1`. |

</details>

---

## What XLS-96 hides, and what it does not

This section is about the **protocol**. Where it describes this project's own demonstration, it says so.

**Hidden.** Individual holder balances, and the amounts moved by confidential transfers.

**Public, always.** The sender and receiver of every transfer; the transaction type; the token; total supply and total confidential supply; the amount of every conversion into or out of confidential form; and the fact and timing of every transfer, so how often anyone transacts.

**Who can decrypt every balance.** The issuer, always: every confidential balance carries a mandatory encrypted mirror under the issuer's key. An auditor too, if one is named. This was executed, not inferred: holder, issuer and auditor each decrypted the same balance, at two different balances (E-58). Registered keys cannot be rotated (E-9), and only one auditor is supported (E-11). Whether naming an auditor can be undone is unknown; this project has not searched for it (P-12).

**What the issuer can do without consent.** If the issuance allows clawback, burn any holder's entire confidential balance; it is destroyed, not credited to anyone (E-12, E-21). This project's issuances allow it, so in every demonstration here the issuer can. And unless an issuance was created with its flags made immutable, which this project's were not, the issuer can also freeze balances by enabling `CanLock` and locking, which `DynamicMPT` allows after creation (E-290, E-292; read at source, not executed).

**Who can spend.** Only the holder of `sk_A`: a `ConfidentialMPTSend` proof cannot be made without it (E-33). Where `sk_A` is derived from the holder's XRPL master seed, whoever holds that seed holds it too. The demonstration does not show holder-only custody, because its facility driver plays every party and holds every seed. And a hostile process running as the same user can read `sk_A` out of memory.

**Lost keys.** If a holder loses `sk_A`, the balance cannot be spent, and XLS-96 has no rotation or recovery (P-10); the only remedy is issuer clawback, which destroys the balance. A key derived from the master seed under this project's own construction can be re-derived from that seed, but the derivation is not a published standard (issue #10).

**A zero balance can be visible.** Encrypted zero is written to a balance field in three cases: the spending balance on first initialisation, the inbox when `MergeInbox` empties it, and the whole position on clawback. Each is recognisable on sight, so enrolment is publicly visible (F-1). A balance spent down to zero holds a randomised encryption of zero and is not recognisable (E-211).

**In short, it hides the shape of the book, not its size.** The float, because converting it into confidential form publishes the amount, every retirement tranche, and every bank–supplier relationship with its timing, so how often each supplier draws, are public. Each supplier's limit and the sizes of its drawdowns and outstanding balance are not; this project once claimed more was hidden (R-1). The public perimeter still bounds the interior by arithmetic: convert in 500, receive nothing, convert back 400, and anyone knows the other 100 is either still held or has left by confidential transfer. [`WHAT-CONFIDENTIAL-MEANS`](docs/explainer/WHAT-CONFIDENTIAL-MEANS-2026-09-02.md) sets this out at length.

**What this is not:** non-custodial, trustless, private from the issuer, or anonymous. It is not audited, not production-ready, and not compliant with any regulation.

### Before opting in

A holder's first `ConfidentialMPTConvert` commits them three ways. The first and third are irreversible; the second lasts while any holder of the issuance has a non-zero confidential balance:

1. It registers an encryption key that **can never be changed**.
2. It blocks deleting their `MPToken`, and so locks its reserve, **while any holder of the issuance has a non-zero confidential balance**. XLS-0096 §7.2 and rippled's source agree: a holder's own deletion fails with `tecHAS_OBLIGATIONS` until the issuance's `ConfidentialOutstandingAmount` is zero, which no single holder controls. Read at XLS-0096 `58ccd30` and rippled 3.3.0, not executed, and not re-read at the 3.4.1 Devnet now runs (F-29, E-316).
3. It publishes the converted amount **in plaintext**.

---

## How it fits together

```
  ONE machine. The demonstration runs every role locally; that is a property
  of the demo, not of the design.
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                                                                        │
 │   web/app          web/api             ┌────────────────────────────┐  │
 │   TanStack Start   Elysia              │  signer/  wconf-signer     │  │
 │   React 19  ──────▶ READ-ONLY   ──────▶│  Rust binary               │  │
 │   :3000      HTTP   :3011        UDS   │                            │  │
 │                        │    Status,    │   ElGamal secret  sk_A     │  │
 │                        │    and only   │   XRPL account key         │  │
 │   facility/            │    Status     │   proof generation         │  │
 │   TypeScript ──────────┼───────────────▶   transaction signing      │  │
 │   holds every          │          UDS  │   per-transaction          │  │
 │   party's seed         │    Pair,      │     confirmation UI        │  │
 │        │               │    Prepare    │   reads, never submits     │  │
 │        │               │               └─────────────┬──────────────┘  │
 └────────┼───────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┘
          │ submits       │ reads                       │ reads
          ▼               ▼                             ▼
          XRPL Devnet — network_id 2, rippled 3.4.1 when read on 2026-10-18
```

The signer answers three requests. `Pair` opens a grant: a named set of operations, valid for a limited time and only on that socket connection. `Prepare` asks for one transaction under a grant; the signer builds it, shows it to the holder and returns the signed bytes. `Status` carries no authority.

- **[`signer/`](signer/)** — a Rust binary on the holder's machine. Each instance holds one participant's `sk_A` and XRPL key; in the demonstration the facility writes each party's profile and starts one signer per party. It builds the proofs and signs, and shows what it is about to sign in its own window, parsed from the transaction it built, so a caller that lies in its request cannot get a different transaction confirmed. It refuses every network but Devnet. It reads the ledger and **never submits**, so whatever submits must set `fail_hard`: a failing confidential transaction applied as a `tec` lands on the ledger with its ciphertexts (F-23, E-149). The flag stops that at the ledger, not at the node the blob was handed to (F-28), and nothing forces a submitter to set it (B-15).
- **[`facility/`](facility/)** — the receivables facility: a Dedicated Account, supplier enrolment, drawdowns, repayments, an off-ledger balance book and retirement in tranches. It is a single-machine test driver that plays the bank, the Dedicated Account and every supplier, so it holds every seed and derives every party's `sk_A` from it. It sends the signer an operation, an issuance, a destination and an amount. The signer refuses a request that carries a seed, key or randomness field; that is a check over a named set of field names, not of what a value contains.
- **[`web/`](web/)** — a **read-only** viewer: `web/api` (Elysia, bound to loopback) and `web/app` (TanStack Start, React 19). It renders public ledger state, the observer's view, and an issuer page drawn from a snapshot that `tools/issuer-view-snapshot.ts` wrote; that page says whether the issuer's decryption succeeded, never the figure (E-241). It asks the signer for `Status` only, which [`tools/check-web-readonly.ts`](tools/check-web-readonly.ts) checks by reading `web/api`'s source; it cannot prove what is sent at run time.
- **[`tools/`](tools/)** — the observer harness; the issuer-view tools, which hold the issuer key (`issuer-view-snapshot.ts` writes the viewer's snapshot, `issuer-decrypt-balance.ts` prints a figure); the live amendment reader; and the repository's checks.

**The signer is a real boundary for the browser, and only for the browser.** No API available to a web page can open a Unix socket, so a script injected into the page cannot open the signer's socket; the most it can reach is `Status`, through `web/api`. That closes the path by construction rather than by an origin check, which any local process can forge. It does not stop an adversary with code execution on the holder's machine. The authority on the design is [`ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-18.md`](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-18.md).

---

## Run it

### The checks

You need [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.3.14, `git` and `make`:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
make ci
```

`make ci` is what GitHub Actions runs: the type check, the TypeScript suites, and the repository checks that need neither the native build nor the local secret store. It checks for secrets by pattern only; the full sweep needs the maintainer's local secret store, and was run on the published commit. It skips the signer's tests and the checks that compile the signer, and reports as skipped the five facility tests that start one. On 2026-10-18 from a fresh clone, and on GitHub's first Linux run on 2026-10-19, it gave 227 pass, 0 fail and 5 skipped.

### The full build

Read the [demo script](docs/explainer/WEB-TIER-DEMO-SCRIPT-2026-08-28.md) first: it says what to show, in what order, and what not to claim. You need a Rust toolchain, `cmake`, `clang`, Homebrew `openssl@3` (the native build is macOS-only today) and network access to Devnet.

```bash
tools/rebuild-env.sh    # builds the patched mpt-crypto into /tmp/wconf
make signer             # cargo build
make web-api            # the read-only viewer: http://127.0.0.1:3011
make web-app            #                       http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

The signer links a patched fork of `mpt-crypto`, and the patch is committed. `make vendor-verify` checks the build tree's pin and which tracked files differ; it does not see untracked files or changes inside the files it allows, and `/tmp/wconf` is writable by any process running as you. Running the signer and the facility needs a holder profile and funded Devnet accounts, which this repository does not tell you how to create; the demo script lists what has to exist first. Walkthroughs: [the facility](docs/explainer/FACILITY-WALKTHROUGH-2026-08-20.md), [the web tier](docs/explainer/WEB-TIER-WALKTHROUGH-2026-08-28.md).

Measured on 2026-10-18: the signer's suite passes 279 tests with none failing; 4 more are ignored by default, three of which read live Devnet. The facility ran 28 validated transactions on Devnet on 2026-08-25, recorded in [`facility/README.md`](facility/README.md).

### Amendment status

This build needs `ConfidentialTransfer`. Read on 2026-10-18 ([snapshot](docs/task-zero/amendments-2026-10-18.json)):

| network | `ConfidentialTransfer` | `PermissionedDomains` | `SingleAssetVault` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Devnet** | **enabled** | enabled | enabled |
| Testnet | supported, not enabled | enabled | supported, not enabled |
| Mainnet | supported, not enabled | enabled | supported, not enabled |

So Devnet is the only network where this can run. Amendment state changes; run `make check-amendments` for a current reading rather than trusting this table (P-3).

---

## What the research found

Seven findings about XLS-96, its reference implementation and its ecosystem: proof sizes and composition, why a large balance can decrypt faster than a small one, and where a confidential balance fails to compose with the ledger's vault and lending primitives. Three correct a reading this project first got wrong. None is a security claim about this project. **→ [`PROTOCOL-FINDINGS`](docs/explainer/PROTOCOL-FINDINGS-2026-09-02.md)**

Observations for the XLS-96 authors collect in [`UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md`](UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md). Eleven have been filed upstream since 2026-08-26; the four since 2026-09-28 were reviewed before filing, under [`docs/UPSTREAM-FILING-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/UPSTREAM-FILING-PROTOCOL.md). Their outcomes were re-surveyed on 2026-10-18 ([survey](docs/evidence/upstream-survey-2026-10-18/README.md)). Found a defect *here*? Open an issue on this repository.

---

## What is open

| open | what it means | tracked in |
|---|---|---|
| **The key derivation is unpublished** | A holder with their master seed but not this repository cannot reconstruct their key; treat it as lock-in until it is published | issue #10 |
| **No run against a local node** | Every Devnet read went to the public cluster, a risk the project owner accepted and recorded | B-15, E-151 |
| **The issuer snapshot is plaintext on disk** | The issuer-view CLI writes decrypted demo balances to a `0600` file, which any process running as the same user can read | E-212, E-241 |
| **Custody** | Accepted by the project owner, not solved: the issuer can erase or freeze the facility's float, and the Dedicated Account's seed both moves the float and decrypts it, so those two powers cannot be held apart (E-266) | B-27, [`CUSTODY`](docs/research/CUSTODY-2026-08-28.md) |
| **The `MPToken` reserve** | How much reserve the opt-in locks is not recorded here | — |
| **`ADR-0002`: the facility as application logic, not XLS-66** | Still `Proposed`, on one research question: whether upstream intends a confidential balance to stay invisible to vault accounting (XRPL-Standards #611) | [`ADR-0002`](docs/decisions/ADR-0002-facility-as-application-logic.md) |
| **Bulletproof blinding** | Whether the Bulletproof's blinding values may be derived deterministically, given that they carry its zero-knowledge property | issue #8 |
| **A frozen-token check before signing** | Whether the signer should detect `terFROZEN` before it signs | B-17 |
