[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) says what contributions are wanted and what a pull request must pass. [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) says how to report a vulnerability. [`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) is the Contributor Covenant.

This project's own work is [Apache 2.0](LICENSE). Material reproduced from third parties is not: a patch against `XRPLF/mpt-crypto`, which carries no licence, and quotations of other projects' source and specifications in the records. [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) lists it, and [`LICENSES/`](LICENSES/) carries the notices it requires.

## Credit

XLS-0096 is the work of Murat Cenk, Aanchal Malhotra, Ayo Akinyele, Peter Chen, Shawn Xie and Yinyi Qian, with the reference cryptography in [`XRPLF/mpt-crypto`](https://github.com/XRPLF/mpt-crypto). The compact sigma protocol behind the send proof's 192 bytes is the work of **Tess Dore and Murat Cenk** at RippleX Research, published separately from XLS-0096.

Upstream's Confidential Transfer implementation was reviewed by **Trail of Bits** in April 2026; several things this repository first recorded as findings turned out to be issues that review had already found and Ripple had fixed. A later revision of that report could not be obtained (B-13). Two further reviews exist whose full findings this project could not obtain: the Sherlock XRP Ledger Attackathon, a contest covering Confidential Transfers (contest 1260, B-30), and a Zellic scan of `mpt-crypto` (B-31); it has read only the findings that upstream issues cite by identifier. Of the three, only Trail of Bits' April report could be checked against this project's findings.

This repository analyses and builds on all of the above; it claims none of it.
16:So every Harmonize-specific question — which signing schemes it offers, whether its policy engine can be extended, what its approval workflow can read — is a **named gap** here rather than an answer. `CLAUDE.md`: *a named gap is a correct output; a substituted source is a corrupted one.*
18:**What this document does instead:** derive from *our* side what the protocol requires of a key holder, and test custodial models against that. Those requirements are properties of XLS-0096 and of this project's ruled key derivation, so they hold against **any** custody platform, named or not. That is a narrower claim than a Harmonize assessment and it is the one the evidence supports.
22:## Finding 1 — the ruled key derivation is incompatible with custodial key management
36:**What would change this:** a derivation whose input is not the master seed, or a custody platform that performs the derivation inside its own boundary and never emits either secret. **The second is not obviously impossible** — it is a key-derivation function over a seed the platform already holds — and it is the question worth putting to a custody vendor. ⚠ **It would require the derivation to be a published standard, which is issue #10, open, and no code discharges it.**
40:## Finding 2 — a policy engine cannot enforce an amount limit on a confidential amount
44:Custodial approval workflows are written over transaction *values*: *"require two approvers above $1M"*, *"block transfers to unlisted counterparties"*, *"cap daily outflow"*. A `ConfidentialMPTSend` carries **a proof, not a value**. The amount is exactly what has been hidden, and it is hidden from *everyone* holding only public data — which includes the policy engine.
50:| policy shape | on a confidential send | why |
52:| *"require N approvers above amount X"* | ⚠ **unevaluable** | the amount is a proof |
53:| *"cap total daily outflow"* | ⚠ **unevaluable** | sums of hidden amounts are hidden |
57:| *"require N approvers, unconditionally"* | **evaluable** | no amount is read |
60:⚠ **The pattern: every policy over an IDENTITY, a TIME or a COUNT survives; every policy over a VALUE does not.** That is P-4 and P-11 restated as a custody constraint — this system hides amounts and hides nothing else — and it is the single most useful sentence in this document for a capital-markets reader.
64:1. **Give the policy engine the ElGamal secret.** Then it can decrypt and evaluate — and it is now a party that can read every balance, which is Finding 1's problem with a second holder added.
65:2. **Have the holder attest the amount alongside the proof.** The engine then enforces a policy over a *claim*, not over the transaction. ⚠ **An attestation the engine cannot verify against the proof is a policy over an honest holder's honesty**, which is not a control.
66:3. **Prove the bound in zero knowledge.** *"This transfer is under $1M"* is a range proof — and **XLS-0096 already carries range proofs**, so the machinery is present rather than hypothetical. Verified at source: a `ConfidentialMPTSend`'s 946-byte proof is 192 B sigma **plus a 754 B aggregated Bulletproof over two 64-bit values**, and a `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack`'s 816 B is 128 B sigma plus a **688 B single Bulletproof**; TASK ZERO records that *"the aggregated Bulletproof proves the amount lies in [0, 2⁶⁴)"* (`docs/task-zero/TASK-ZERO-2026-08-13.md`, Grade A, sizes confirmed by execution against `mpt-crypto`).
68:   ⚠ **What is present is a range proof over a FIXED bound — [0, 2⁶⁴), the field's own validity condition — not over a POLICY bound chosen by an approver.** Those are different proofs: one is a protocol invariant every transaction already carries, the other is a per-policy statement nobody has specified, generated by the holder, verified by the engine, and bound to the same amount the transaction moves. ⚠ **This project has neither built nor costed the second, and the gap between them is the whole question.** Recorded as a direction, not a recommendation.
76:`MPTAmount` is a **plaintext field on every individual `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack`**, so retiring a position in tranches publishes **every tranche size** and its timing. `CLAIMS.md` **F-24**, found in this project's own facility walkthrough after that document had already passed `claims-check`, and read off two validated Devnet transactions at 95 and 191.
101:- **That the tension is unresolvable.** Finding 2's third way out — range proofs over policy bounds — is a real direction that this project has not costed.
110:2. Can the policy engine consume a **range proof over a policy bound** rather than a value? ⚠ Note the protocol's existing Bulletproofs prove a **fixed** range, not a chosen one — the two are not the same artifact. (Finding 2's third way out.)
14://!   signer-side state. Its fields are private.
39://! **decrypts `SenderEncryptedAmount` from the transaction itself**, with the
137:/// Built by the signer, from the signer's own state. Fields are private on

530:    /// Whether this transaction carries an `AuditorEncryptedAmount`.
556:    /// `DestinationTag`, or a `MPTAmount` on a Send, rode along unrendered and
652:                     approve",

/** Default places the project keeps secrets. `rebuild-env.sh` and `facility/` write these. */
export function defaultStorePaths(): string[] {
  const p = [join(homedir(), ".wconf"), "/tmp/wconf"];
  if (process.env.WCONF_STATE_BACKUP) p.unshift(process.env.WCONF_STATE_BACKUP);
  return p;
}

export function loadStore(paths: string[], env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env): Store {
  const st: Store = { files: [], needles: [], secrets: 0, publicSkipped: 0 };
  const files: string[] = [];
  for (const p of paths) {
    if (!existsSync(p)) continue;
    const s = lstatSync(p);
    if (s.isFile()) files.push(p);
    else if (s.isDirectory()) for (const n of readdirSync(p)) if (n.includes(".json") && lstatSync(join(p, n)).isFile()) files.push(join(p, n));
  }
  // Counted by distinct VALUE: the same seed in two copies of state.json is one
  // secret, and a count that doubled it would claim coverage it does not have.
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const addSeed = (seed: string, label: string) => {
    const d = decodeSeedLike(seed);
    if (!d || !d.checksumOk) return;
    if (publicEntropyRule(d.entropy)) { st.publicSkipped++; return; }
    if (seen.has(seed)) return;
    seen.add(seed);
    st.secrets++;
    st.needles.push(...needlesForSeed(seed, label));
  };
  const addHex = (v: string, label: string) => {
    const k = v.toLowerCase();
    if (seen.has(k)) return;
    seen.add(k);
    st.secrets++;
    st.needles.push({ value: k, label, kind: "hex" });
  };
  for (const f of files) {
    st.files.push(f);
    const raw = readFileSync(f, "utf8");
    const name = f.slice(f.lastIndexOf("/") + 1);
    let json: unknown;
    // ⚠ A malformed store file REFUSES (`REVIEW-056` S3-3). It used to fall back
    // to scanning the raw text for seeds, which silently dropped every 64-hex
    // scalar in it — the one shape only this class can find — while another
    // file kept the store non-empty, so no refusal fired.
    try { json = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) {
      throw new Error(`store file ${f} is not valid JSON (${String(e).slice(0, 80)}); the known-value class cannot tell its secrets from its hashes, so it refuses rather than guess`);
    }
    const walk = (o: unknown, path: string) => {
      if (Array.isArray(o)) o.forEach((v, i) => walk(v, `${path}[${i}]`));
      else if (o && typeof o === "object") for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o)) walk(v, `${path}.${k}`);
      else if (typeof o === "string") {
        const key = path.slice(path.lastIndexOf(".") + 1).replace(/\[\d+\]$/, "");
        if (decodeSeedLike(o)?.checksumOk) addSeed(o, `${name}:${path}`);
        else if (/^[0-9A-Fa-f]{64}$/.test(o) && components(key).some((c) => SECRET_COMPONENTS.has(c))) addHex(o, `${name}:${path}`);
      }
    };
    walk(json, "");
  }
  const envSk = env.WCONF_ELGAMAL_SK?.trim();
  if (envSk && /^[0-9A-Fa-f]{64}$/.test(envSk)) addHex(envSk, "environment: WCONF_ELGAMAL_SK");
  return st;
}

const HEXRUN = /[0-9A-Fa-f]{24,}/g;
export function knownHits(text: string, store: Store): Hit[] {
  if (!store.needles.length) return [];
  const out: Hit[] = [];
  // ⚠ Each hex needle is searched WITHOUT its leading zeros, so a stored secret
  // printed unpadded, as `BigInt.toString(16)` prints one in sixteen, is still
  // found; the padded form contains the unpadded one. Found from round three's
  // R3-1, which showed the shape rule's tail but not this class's.
  const hexN = store.needles.filter((n) => n.kind === "hex").map((n) => ({ ...n, value: n.value.replace(/^0+/, "") || n.value }));
  const b58N = store.needles.filter((n) => n.kind === "b58");
  for (const m of text.matchAll(HEXRUN)) {
    const run = m[0].toLowerCase();
    for (const n of hexN) {
      const k = run.indexOf(n.value);
      if (k !== -1) out.push({ cls: "known-value", at: m.index! + k, len: n.value.length, shown: n.label, why: "a value from the local secret store" });
    }
  }
  if (b58N.length) {

allowed (each rule, and how many hits it permitted):

What this gate does NOT catch (each is an asserted-uncaught control):
  - a secret split across two string literals or two lines
  - a secret in UTF-16, base64, gzip or any other re-encoding
  - an unlabelled 64-hex ElGamal secret that is NOT in the local store (no shape rule can tell it from a hash)
  - a seed or key in RFC 1751 words, or as a decimal or byte array
  - a home path under a user name on the generic list
  - a labelled scalar printed in fewer than 48 hex digits: a uniform key is that short with probability below 2^-64
  - a secret listed as an array element under a label, rather than as the value of a key
  - gitignored files, the reflog and unreachable objects: none of them is published
  - a hostname, a machine serial, or a person's name — only paths and email addresses are personal-data classes

# W-CONF

### A Confidential MPT reference application for the XRP Ledger.

*Built to find out what XLS-96 actually hides — by execution, not by reading.*

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-3b82f6)](LICENSE)
[![Network](https://img.shields.io/badge/network-Devnet%20only-e11d48)](#amendment-status)
[![Spec](https://img.shields.io/badge/XLS--0096-Final-22c55e)](https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/tree/master/XLS-0096-confidential-mpt)
[![Signer](https://img.shields.io/badge/signer-Rust-000000?logo=rust&logoColor=white)](signer/)
[![Runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-Bun-000000?logo=bun&logoColor=white)](https://bun.sh)
[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-research%20artifact-6366f1)](#what-is-open)

[**What it hides**](#what-xls-96-hides-and-what-it-does-not) · [**Run it**](#run-it) · [**Findings**](docs/explainer/PROTOCOL-FINDINGS-2026-09-02.md) · [**What is open**](#what-is-open) · [**Claims register**](CLAIMS.md)

</div>

---

> **Public history starts at publication.** This repository was developed privately from 2026-08-16 and published on 2026-10-19 as two commits: the tree, and its revision log regenerated from this history. The commit hashes cited in `CLAIMS.md` and `docs/reviews/` refer to that private archive and do not resolve here. Issues #1 to #13 were copied from the archive in order, so the issue numbers cited here resolve; the ten closed ones are stubs.

**A confidential receivables facility on the XRP Ledger.** A bank opens a facility; suppliers enrol, draw down against invoices and repay; the facility retires in tranches. Every position is an encrypted balance on a public ledger. It has run on Devnet, and the point of building it was to establish exactly what an outside observer sees while it does.

**The short answer: XLS-96 hides balances and the amounts of confidential transfers, and nothing else, and even a balance is recognisable when it holds the canonical encrypted zero.** Converting into or out of confidential form publishes the amount in plaintext. Who pays whom, when and how often is public. The issuer can decrypt every balance. The details, with evidence, are [below](#what-xls-96-hides-and-what-it-does-not).

> ⚠ **Devnet only. No mainnet writes, at any phase.** This repository has not been audited, is not production-ready, and is not safe to put value behind.

It exercises Multi-Purpose Tokens (XLS-33) and Confidential Transfers (XLS-96, specified in the document XLS-0096, `Final` since 2026-09-03, read on 2026-10-18: E-1) together. It does not use Credentials (XLS-70) or Permissioned Domains (XLS-80).

> **Citations.** Ids such as *(E-58)* point to rows of [`CLAIMS.md`](CLAIMS.md), the register that governs what this project may claim: **E** is established evidence, **F** a finding, **P** a standing prohibition, **B** a blocker, open or ruled, and **R** a correction to something this project claimed earlier. Where this README and a row disagree, the row wins. Bare issue numbers are issues on this repository.

<details>
<summary><b>Terms, if you are new to XLS-96 or the XRPL</b></summary>

| term | meaning here |
|---|---|
| **MPT** | Multi-Purpose Token (XLS-33). `MPTokenIssuance` defines a token; an `MPToken` is one holder's position in it. |
| **Confidential balance** | A balance held as an ElGamal ciphertext on the ledger. Each holder has two: a *spending* balance and an *inbox* that receives transfers, folded in by `ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox`. |
| **`sk_A`** | A holder's ElGamal secret key. It decrypts that holder's balance and is needed to prove a `ConfidentialMPTSend`. |
| **Convert / Send / ConvertBack** | `ConfidentialMPTConvert` moves plaintext into confidential form, `ConfidentialMPTSend` moves a hidden amount between holders, `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack` moves it back out. Only Send hides its amount. |
| **Encrypted zero (`EncZero`)** | The canonical ciphertext of zero, which anyone can recompute. It is written on first initialisation, merge reset and clawback only. |
| **Proofs** | `Send` carries a 192-byte compact sigma proof and a 754-byte aggregated Bulletproof; `ConvertBack` a 128-byte sigma and a 688-byte Bulletproof; `Convert` and `Clawback` a 64-byte proof each; `MergeInbox` none. |
| **`tec` codes** | A `tec` result is *applied to the ledger*: it consumes a sequence number and its fields persist, ciphertexts included. |
| **`fail_hard`** | The submission parameter that asks a node to discard a failing transaction instead of applying it. Internal documents here use `tapFailHard` as shorthand for it; see [`docs/VOCABULARY.md`](docs/VOCABULARY.md). |
| **Dedicated Account** | The facility's own holding account. It is not an XLS-65 `Vault`, which cannot hold confidential balances. |
| **UDS** | Unix domain socket, a local channel no browser API can open. |
| **Loopback** | A node or service on the same machine, reached at `127.0.0.1`. |

</details>

---

## What XLS-96 hides, and what it does not

This section is about the **protocol**. Where it describes this project's own demonstration, it says so.

**Hidden.** Individual holder balances, and the amounts moved by confidential transfers.

**Public, always.** The sender and receiver of every transfer; the transaction type; the token; total supply and total confidential supply; the amount of every conversion into or out of confidential form; and the fact and timing of every transfer, so how often anyone transacts.

**Who can decrypt every balance.** The issuer, always: every confidential balance carries a mandatory encrypted mirror under the issuer's key. An auditor too, if one is named. This was executed, not inferred: holder, issuer and auditor each decrypted the same balance, at two different balances (E-58). Registered keys cannot be rotated (E-9), and only one auditor is supported (E-11). Whether naming an auditor can be undone is unknown; this project has not searched for it (P-12).

**What the issuer can do without consent.** If the issuance allows clawback, burn any holder's entire confidential balance; it is destroyed, not credited to anyone (E-12, E-21). This project's issuances allow it, so in every demonstration here the issuer can. And unless an issuance was created with its flags made immutable, which this project's were not, the issuer can also freeze balances by enabling `CanLock` and locking, which `DynamicMPT` allows after creation (E-290, E-292; read at source, not executed).

**Who can spend.** Only the holder of `sk_A`: a `ConfidentialMPTSend` proof cannot be made without it (E-33). Where `sk_A` is derived from the holder's XRPL master seed, whoever holds that seed holds it too. The demonstration does not show holder-only custody, because its facility driver plays every party and holds every seed. And a hostile process running as the same user can read `sk_A` out of memory.

**Lost keys.** If a holder loses `sk_A`, the balance cannot be spent, and XLS-96 has no rotation or recovery (P-10); the only remedy is issuer clawback, which destroys the balance. A key derived from the master seed under this project's own construction can be re-derived from that seed, but the derivation is not a published standard (issue #10).

**A zero balance can be visible.** Encrypted zero is written to a balance field in three cases: the spending balance on first initialisation, the inbox when `MergeInbox` empties it, and the whole position on clawback. Each is recognisable on sight, so enrolment is publicly visible (F-1). A balance spent down to zero holds a randomised encryption of zero and is not recognisable (E-211).

**In short, it hides the shape of the book, not its size.** The float, because converting it into confidential form publishes the amount, every retirement tranche, and every bank–supplier relationship with its timing, so how often each supplier draws, are public. Each supplier's limit and the sizes of its drawdowns and outstanding balance are not; this project once claimed more was hidden (R-1). The public perimeter still bounds the interior by arithmetic: convert in 500, receive nothing, convert back 400, and anyone knows the other 100 is either still held or has left by confidential transfer. [`WHAT-CONFIDENTIAL-MEANS`](docs/explainer/WHAT-CONFIDENTIAL-MEANS-2026-09-02.md) sets this out at length.

**What this is not:** non-custodial, trustless, private from the issuer, or anonymous. It is not audited, not production-ready, and not compliant with any regulation.

### Before opting in

A holder's first `ConfidentialMPTConvert` commits them three ways. The first and third are irreversible; the second lasts while any holder of the issuance has a non-zero confidential balance:

1. It registers an encryption key that **can never be changed**.
2. It blocks deleting their `MPToken`, and so locks its reserve, **while any holder of the issuance has a non-zero confidential balance**. XLS-0096 §7.2 and rippled's source agree: a holder's own deletion fails with `tecHAS_OBLIGATIONS` until the issuance's `ConfidentialOutstandingAmount` is zero, which no single holder controls. Read at XLS-0096 `58ccd30` and rippled 3.3.0, not executed, and not re-read at the 3.4.1 Devnet now runs (F-29, E-316).
3. It publishes the converted amount **in plaintext**.

---

## How it fits together

```
  ONE machine. The demonstration runs every role locally; that is a property
  of the demo, not of the design.
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                                                                        │
 │   web/app          web/api             ┌────────────────────────────┐  │
 │   TanStack Start   Elysia              │  signer/  wconf-signer     │  │
 │   React 19  ──────▶ READ-ONLY   ──────▶│  Rust binary               │  │
 │   :3000      HTTP   :3011        UDS   │                            │  │
 │                        │    Status,    │   ElGamal secret  sk_A     │  │
 │                        │    and only   │   XRPL account key         │  │
 │   facility/            │    Status     │   proof generation         │  │
 │   TypeScript ──────────┼───────────────▶   transaction signing      │  │
 │   holds every          │          UDS  │   per-transaction          │  │
 │   party's seed         │    Pair,      │     confirmation UI        │  │
 │        │               │    Prepare    │   reads, never submits     │  │
 │        │               │               └─────────────┬──────────────┘  │
 └────────┼───────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┘
          │ submits       │ reads                       │ reads
          ▼               ▼                             ▼
          XRPL Devnet — network_id 2, rippled 3.4.1 when read on 2026-10-18
```

The signer answers three requests. `Pair` opens a grant: a named set of operations, valid for a limited time and only on that socket connection. `Prepare` asks for one transaction under a grant; the signer builds it, shows it to the holder and returns the signed bytes. `Status` carries no authority.

- **[`signer/`](signer/)** — a Rust binary on the holder's machine. Each instance holds one participant's `sk_A` and XRPL key; in the demonstration the facility writes each party's profile and starts one signer per party. It builds the proofs and signs, and shows what it is about to sign in its own window, parsed from the transaction it built, so a caller that lies in its request cannot get a different transaction confirmed. It refuses every network but Devnet. It reads the ledger and **never submits**, so whatever submits must set `fail_hard`: a failing confidential transaction applied as a `tec` lands on the ledger with its ciphertexts (F-23, E-149). The flag stops that at the ledger, not at the node the blob was handed to (F-28), and nothing forces a submitter to set it (B-15).
- **[`facility/`](facility/)** — the receivables facility: a Dedicated Account, supplier enrolment, drawdowns, repayments, an off-ledger balance book and retirement in tranches. It is a single-machine test driver that plays the bank, the Dedicated Account and every supplier, so it holds every seed and derives every party's `sk_A` from it. It sends the signer an operation, an issuance, a destination and an amount. The signer refuses a request that carries a seed, key or randomness field; that is a check over a named set of field names, not of what a value contains.
- **[`web/`](web/)** — a **read-only** viewer: `web/api` (Elysia, bound to loopback) and `web/app` (TanStack Start, React 19). It renders public ledger state, the observer's view, and an issuer page drawn from a snapshot that `tools/issuer-view-snapshot.ts` wrote; that page says whether the issuer's decryption succeeded, never the figure (E-241). It asks the signer for `Status` only, which [`tools/check-web-readonly.ts`](tools/check-web-readonly.ts) checks by reading `web/api`'s source; it cannot prove what is sent at run time.
- **[`tools/`](tools/)** — the observer harness; the issuer-view tools, which hold the issuer key (`issuer-view-snapshot.ts` writes the viewer's snapshot, `issuer-decrypt-balance.ts` prints a figure); the live amendment reader; and the repository's checks.

**The signer is a real boundary for the browser, and only for the browser.** No API available to a web page can open a Unix socket, so a script injected into the page cannot open the signer's socket; the most it can reach is `Status`, through `web/api`. That closes the path by construction rather than by an origin check, which any local process can forge. It does not stop an adversary with code execution on the holder's machine. The authority on the design is [`ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-18.md`](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-18.md).

---

## Run it

### The checks

You need [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.3.14, `git` and `make`:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
make ci
```

`make ci` is what GitHub Actions runs: the type check, the TypeScript suites, and the repository checks that need neither the native build nor the local secret store. It checks for secrets by pattern only; the full sweep needs the maintainer's local secret store, and was run on the published commit. It skips the signer's tests and the checks that compile the signer, and reports as skipped the five facility tests that start one. On 2026-10-18 from a fresh clone, and on GitHub's first Linux run on 2026-10-19, it gave 227 pass, 0 fail and 5 skipped.

### The full build

Read the [demo script](docs/explainer/WEB-TIER-DEMO-SCRIPT-2026-08-28.md) first: it says what to show, in what order, and what not to claim. You need a Rust toolchain, `cmake`, `clang`, Homebrew `openssl@3` (the native build is macOS-only today) and network access to Devnet.

```bash
tools/rebuild-env.sh    # builds the patched mpt-crypto into /tmp/wconf
make signer             # cargo build
make web-api            # the read-only viewer: http://127.0.0.1:3011
make web-app            #                       http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

The signer links a patched fork of `mpt-crypto`, and the patch is committed. `make vendor-verify` checks the build tree's pin and which tracked files differ; it does not see untracked files or changes inside the files it allows, and `/tmp/wconf` is writable by any process running as you. Running the signer and the facility needs a holder profile and funded Devnet accounts, which this repository does not tell you how to create; the demo script lists what has to exist first. Walkthroughs: [the facility](docs/explainer/FACILITY-WALKTHROUGH-2026-08-20.md), [the web tier](docs/explainer/WEB-TIER-WALKTHROUGH-2026-08-28.md).

Measured on 2026-10-18: the signer's suite passes 279 tests with none failing; 4 more are ignored by default, three of which read live Devnet. The facility ran 28 validated transactions on Devnet on 2026-08-25, recorded in [`facility/README.md`](facility/README.md).

### Amendment status

This build needs `ConfidentialTransfer`. Read on 2026-10-18 ([snapshot](docs/task-zero/amendments-2026-10-18.json)):

| network | `ConfidentialTransfer` | `PermissionedDomains` | `SingleAssetVault` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Devnet** | **enabled** | enabled | enabled |
| Testnet | supported, not enabled | enabled | supported, not enabled |
| Mainnet | supported, not enabled | enabled | supported, not enabled |

So Devnet is the only network where this can run. Amendment state changes; run `make check-amendments` for a current reading rather than trusting this table (P-3).

---

## What the research found

Seven findings about XLS-96, its reference implementation and its ecosystem: proof sizes and composition, why a large balance can decrypt faster than a small one, and where a confidential balance fails to compose with the ledger's vault and lending primitives. Three correct a reading this project first got wrong. None is a security claim about this project. **→ [`PROTOCOL-FINDINGS`](docs/explainer/PROTOCOL-FINDINGS-2026-09-02.md)**

Observations for the XLS-96 authors collect in [`UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md`](UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md). Eleven have been filed upstream since 2026-08-26; the four since 2026-09-28 were reviewed before filing, under [`docs/UPSTREAM-FILING-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/UPSTREAM-FILING-PROTOCOL.md). Their outcomes were re-surveyed on 2026-10-18 ([survey](docs/evidence/upstream-survey-2026-10-18/README.md)). Found a defect *here*? Open an issue on this repository.

---

## What is open

| open | what it means | tracked in |
|---|---|---|
| **The key derivation is unpublished** | A holder with their master seed but not this repository cannot reconstruct their key; treat it as lock-in until it is published | issue #10 |
| **No run against a local node** | Every Devnet read went to the public cluster, a risk the project owner accepted and recorded | B-15, E-151 |
| **The issuer snapshot is plaintext on disk** | The issuer-view CLI writes decrypted demo balances to a `0600` file, which any process running as the same user can read | E-212, E-241 |
| **Custody** | Accepted by the project owner, not solved: the issuer can erase or freeze the facility's float, and the Dedicated Account's seed both moves the float and decrypts it, so those two powers cannot be held apart (E-266) | B-27, [`CUSTODY`](docs/research/CUSTODY-2026-08-28.md) |
| **The `MPToken` reserve** | How much reserve the opt-in locks is not recorded here | — |
| **`ADR-0002`: the facility as application logic, not XLS-66** | Still `Proposed`, on one research question: whether upstream intends a confidential balance to stay invisible to vault accounting (XRPL-Standards #611) | [`ADR-0002`](docs/decisions/ADR-0002-facility-as-application-logic.md) |
| **Bulletproof blinding** | Whether the Bulletproof's blinding values may be derived deterministically, given that they carry its zero-knowledge property | issue #8 |
| **A frozen-token check before signing** | Whether the signer should detect `terFROZEN` before it signs | B-17 |

---

## Repository map

```
signer/            the holder signer (Rust): proofs, signing, key derivation
facility/          the confidential receivables facility (TypeScript)
web/api, web/app   the read-only viewer
tools/             the observer harness, the issuer-view CLI and the checks
docs/              architecture, decisions, explainers, research and review records
CLAIMS.md          the claims register: read it before quoting anything here
NOTICE             third-party material, which the Apache licence does not cover
```

`docs/reviews/` keeps this project's own review rounds as written, including the ones that found it wrong, with personal data and test secrets redacted where they appeared. They are not audits.

## Contributing, security and licence

[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) says what contributions are wanted and what a pull request must pass. [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) says how to report a vulnerability. [`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) is the Contributor Covenant.

This project's own work is [Apache 2.0](LICENSE). Material reproduced from third parties is not: a patch against `XRPLF/mpt-crypto`, which carries no licence, and quotations of other projects' source and specifications in the records. [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) lists it, and [`LICENSES/`](LICENSES/) carries the notices it requires.

## Credit

XLS-0096 is the work of Murat Cenk, Aanchal Malhotra, Ayo Akinyele, Peter Chen, Shawn Xie and Yinyi Qian, with the reference cryptography in [`XRPLF/mpt-crypto`](https://github.com/XRPLF/mpt-crypto). The compact sigma protocol behind the send proof's 192 bytes is the work of **Tess Dore and Murat Cenk** at RippleX Research, published separately from XLS-0096.

Upstream's Confidential Transfer implementation was reviewed by **Trail of Bits** in April 2026; several things this repository first recorded as findings turned out to be issues that review had already found and Ripple had fixed. A later revision of that report could not be obtained (B-13). Two further reviews exist whose full findings this project could not obtain: the Sherlock XRP Ledger Attackathon, a contest covering Confidential Transfers (contest 1260, B-30), and a Zellic scan of `mpt-crypto` (B-31); it has read only the findings that upstream issues cite by identifier. Of the three, only Trail of Bits' April report could be checked against this project's findings.

This repository analyses and builds on all of the above; it claims none of it.

    58	/** The source tree, exported into `dest`: a commit's archive, or a trial's working tree. */
    59	function exportSource(repo: string, dest: string, worktree: boolean, commit?: string): string {
    60	  mkdirSync(dest, { recursive: true });
    61	  if (worktree) {
    62	    const files = run(["git", "-C", repo, "ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"]).split("\0").filter(Boolean);
    63	    for (const f of files) if (existsSync(join(repo, f))) cpSync(join(repo, f), join(dest, f), { recursive: false, dereference: false });
    64	    return run(["git", "-C", repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"]).trim();
    65	  }
    66	  const full = run(["git", "-C", repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", `${commit}^{commit}`]).trim();
    67	  const tar = Bun.spawnSync(["git", "-C", repo, "archive", "--format=tar", full], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
    68	  if (tar.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`git archive failed: ${tar.stderr.toString()}`);
    69	  run(["tar", "-x", "-C", dest], { stdin: tar.stdout });
    70	  return full;
    71	}

    73	/** Inside the container. `set -eu`, and the store checks come before anything third-party runs. */
    74	// ⚠ One command per line: `set -e` does not stop on a failure inside an `&&`
    75	// list, and the first version ran the next step after Vite had failed.
    76	const CONTAINER_SCRIPT = [
    77	  "set -eu",
    78	  'for p in /tmp/wconf "$HOME/.wconf"; do if [ -e "$p" ]; then echo "REFUSED: $p exists inside the build container" >&2; exit 3; fi; done',
    79	  "bun install --frozen-lockfile",
    80	  "mkdir -p web/hosted/.build",

    82	  "cd web/app",
    83	  "bunx vite build --config vite.hosted.config.ts",
    84	  "cd /src",
    85	  "bun run web/hosted/vercel-output.ts web/app/dist/client web/hosted/.build",
    86	].join("\n");

    88	/** Build (or reuse) the image named by the Dockerfile's hash. */
    89	function image(): string {
    90	  const tag = `wconf-hosted-build:${createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(DOCKERFILE)).digest("hex").slice(0, 16)}`;
    91	  const have = Bun.spawnSync(["docker", "--context", DOCKER_CONTEXT, "image", "inspect", tag], { stdout: "ignore", stderr: "ignore" });
    92	  if (have.exitCode !== 0) run(["docker", "--context", DOCKER_CONTEXT, "build", "-q", "-t", tag, "-f", DOCKERFILE, import.meta.dir]);
    93	  return tag;
    94	}

    96	export async function build(argv: string[]) {
    97	  const a = args(argv);
    98	  const out = resolve(a.out);
    99	  if (!isAbsolute(out)) throw new Error("--out must resolve to an absolute path");
   100	  if (existsSync(join(out, ".vercel"))) throw new Error(`${out}/.vercel exists; use a fresh --out for each build`);
   101	  const repoTop = run(["git", "-C", a.repo, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"]).trim();
   102	  if (out.startsWith(repoTop + "/")) throw new Error("--out must be outside the repository, so no build file lands in a tree that can be committed");
   103	
   104	  const work = join(out, "work");
   105	  const src = join(work, "src");
   106	  const commit = exportSource(repoTop, src, a.worktree, a.commit);
   107	  const canaries = { VITE_WCONF_CANARY: randomBytes(12).toString("hex"), WCONF_CANARY: randomBytes(12).toString("hex") };
   108	  const env: Record<string, string> = {
   109	    WCONF_ACCEPT_REMOTE_LEDGER_RISK: RISK_ACCEPTANCE_PHRASE,
   110	    WCONF_HOSTED_COMMIT: commit,
   111	    WCONF_HOSTED_CANONICAL_URL: a.canonicalUrl,
   112	    ...canaries,
   113	  };
   114	  const IMAGE = image();
   115	  const docker = [
   116	    "docker", "--context", DOCKER_CONTEXT, "run", "--rm",
   117	    "-v", `${src}:/src`, "-w", "/src",
   118	    ...Object.entries(env).flatMap(([k, v]) => ["-e", `${k}=${v}`]),
   119	    IMAGE, "sh", "-c", CONTAINER_SCRIPT,
   120	  ];
   121	  console.log(`building ${commit}${a.worktree ? " (TRIAL: working tree)" : ""} in ${IMAGE}`);
   122	  const r = Bun.spawnSync(docker, { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
   123	  writeFileSync(join(out, "container.log"), r.stdout.toString() + "\n--- stderr ---\n" + r.stderr.toString());
   124	  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`the container build failed (${r.exitCode}); see ${join(out, "container.log")}`);
   125	
   126	  cpSync(join(src, "web/hosted/.build/.vercel"), join(out, ".vercel"), { recursive: true });
   127	  const snapshot = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(src, "web/hosted/.build/snapshot.json"), "utf8"));
   128	
   129	  // The canaries: neither value may appear anywhere in what is uploaded.
   130	  const leaked = leakedCanaries(join(out, ".vercel"), Object.values(canaries));
   131	  if (leaked.length) throw new Error(`a build variable reached the output (REVIEW-058 M11): ${leaked.join(", ")}`);
   132	
   133	  const manifest = {
   134	    trial: a.worktree,
   135	    commit,
   136	    image: IMAGE,

   145	      "it checked /tmp/wconf and ~/.wconf absent before installing; no deployment token was present",
   125	      for (const e of ev.filter((e) => e.method === "Network.requestWillBeSent")) {

   127	        const u = e.params.request.url as string;
   128	        if (!u.startsWith(origin + "/")) problems.push(`/${page}: a request to ${u}`);
   129	      }
   130	      const violations = await evalJs("window.__violations");
   131	      for (const v of violations ?? []) problems.push(`/${page}: CSP violation ${v}`);
   132	      for (const e of ev.filter((e) => e.method === "Runtime.exceptionThrown")) problems.push(`/${page}: exception ${e.params.exceptionDetails?.exception?.description ?? e.params.exceptionDetails?.text}`);
   133	      for (const e of ev.filter((e) => e.method === "Log.entryAdded" && e.params.entry.level === "error")) {
   134	        const t: string = e.params.entry.text ?? "";
   135	        // Two same-origin 404s are expected: the verdict file before the gate
   136	        // has written it, and the favicon a browser asks for unprompted.
   137	        if (!(/404/.test(t) && /\/(gate-verdict\.json|favicon\.ico)$/.test(e.params.entry.url ?? ""))) problems.push(`/${page}: console error ${t} (${e.params.entry.url ?? "no url"})`);
   138	      }
   139	      const slot = await evalJs("document.querySelector('[data-gate-verdict]')?.textContent ?? null");

   141	      // With a verdict file beside the pages, the footer must show the pass it records.
   142	      if (slot !== null && existsSync(join(root, ".vercel/output/static/gate-verdict.json")) && !/^PASS, /.test(slot)) problems.push(`/${page}: a verdict file exists and the footer shows ${JSON.stringify(slot)}`);
   143	      if (slot === null) problems.push(`/${page}: no gate-verdict slot`);
   144	      else if (/^not loaded/.test(slot)) problems.push(`/${page}: the page's script never ran (the verdict slot still reads ${JSON.stringify(slot)})`);
   145	    }
   146	
   147	    // Client-side navigation: one link, no new document, the target renders.
   148	    await s("Page.navigate", { url: `${origin}/` });
   149	    await sleep(1500);
   150	    const docsBefore = cdp.events.filter((e) => e.method === "Network.requestWillBeSent" && e.params.type === "Document").length;
   151	    await evalJs("document.querySelector('a[href=\"/observer\"]').click()");
   152	    await sleep(1200);
   153	    const docsAfter = cdp.events.filter((e) => e.method === "Network.requestWillBeSent" && e.params.type === "Document").length;
   154	    const path = await evalJs("location.pathname");
   155	    const rendered = await evalJs("document.body.innerText.includes('Observer view: ')");
   156	    if (path !== "/observer" || !rendered) problems.push(`client navigation to /observer did not render (path ${path}, rendered ${rendered})`);
   157	    if (docsAfter !== docsBefore) problems.push("client navigation loaded a new document; the router did not hydrate");
   158	    cdp.close();

   160	    chrome.kill();
   161	    server.stop(true);
   162	    rmSync(profile, { recursive: true, force: true });
   163	  }
   164	  return { problems, pages: HOSTED_PAGES.length, requests, footer };

   168	 * The check's own controls, each a broken copy of a good output run through the

   171	 * violation detector fires instead; this control is for the request detector.
   172	 */
   173	export async function selfTest(root: string): Promise<string[]> {
   174	  const failed: string[] = [];
   175	  const copy = () => { const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "wconf-browser-self-test-")); cpSync(join(root, ".vercel"), join(d, ".vercel"), { recursive: true }); return d; };
   176	  const dirs: string[] = [];
   177	  const elsewhere = Bun.serve({ hostname: "127.0.0.1", port: 0, fetch: () => new Response("x") });
   178	  try {
   155	    for (const m of text(files.get(p)!).matchAll(/\bhttps?:\/\/[A-Za-z0-9.:/#_-]+/g)) {
   156	      const u = m[0].replace(/[.:]+$/, "");
   157	      if (!ADMITTED_URLS.some(([re]) => re.test(u))) add("urls", `${p} names ${u}`);
   158	    }
   159	  }
   160	
   161	  // 6. The Content Security Policy, as config.json delivers it.
   162	  const first = config?.routes?.[0];
   163	  const csp: string | undefined = first?.src === "/(.*)" && first?.continue === true ? first?.headers?.["Content-Security-Policy"] : undefined;
   164	  if (!csp) add("csp", "the first route does not set a Content-Security-Policy on every path");
   165	  else {
   166	    const dirs = new Map(csp.split(";").map((d) => d.trim()).filter(Boolean).map((d) => { const [k, ...v] = d.split(/\s+/); return [k, v] as const; }));
   167	    const exact: Record<string, string[]> = {
   168	      "default-src": ["'self'"], "style-src": ["'self'"], "img-src": ["'self'"], "font-src": ["'self'"],
   169	      "connect-src": ["'self'"], "object-src": ["'none'"], "base-uri": ["'none'"], "form-action": ["'none'"], "frame-ancestors": ["'none'"],
   170	    };
   171	    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(exact)) if (JSON.stringify(dirs.get(k) ?? null) !== JSON.stringify(v)) add("csp", `${k} is ${JSON.stringify(dirs.get(k) ?? null)}, not ${v.join(" ")}`);
   172	    for (const k of dirs.keys()) if (!(k in exact) && k !== "script-src") add("csp", `an unexpected directive ${k}`);
   173	    const script = dirs.get("script-src") ?? [];
   174	    if (script[0] !== "'self'") add("csp", "script-src does not start with 'self'");
   175	    const allowed = new Set(script.slice(1));
   176	    for (const tok of allowed) if (!/^'sha256-[A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*'$/.test(tok)) add("csp", `script-src admits ${tok}`);
   177	    const needed = new Set([...html.values()].flatMap((h) => inlineScripts(h).map(scriptHash)));
   178	    for (const h of needed) if (!allowed.has(h)) add("csp", `an inline script's hash ${h} is not admitted, so the page would not run`);
   179	    for (const h of allowed) if (!needed.has(h)) add("csp", `script-src admits ${h}, which no page carries`);
   180	    for (const [h, v] of Object.entries({ "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff", "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer" })) if (first.headers?.[h] !== v) add("csp", `${h} is not ${v}`);
   181	  }
   182	  for (const [p, h] of html) if (/\sstyle="|<style[\s>]/.test(h)) add("csp", `${p} carries inline style, which style-src 'self' refuses`);
   183	
   184	  // 7. No input that asks a visitor for anything.
   185	  for (const [p, h] of html) if (FORMS.test(h)) add("no-inputs", `${p} renders a form control`);
   186	
   187	  // 8. Every page that renders a ledger value renders the wording, the network check and the index.
   188	  const indices = new Set<string>();
   189	  for (const [p, h] of html) {
   190	    if (!h.includes("data-ledger-value")) continue;
   191	    const plain = decodeEntities(h);
   192	    for (const para of DH2_WORDING) if (!plain.includes(para)) add("ledger-wording", `${p} renders a ledger value without the D-H2 sentence beginning ${JSON.stringify(para.slice(0, 40))}`);
   193	    if (!h.includes(`data-network-id="${DEVNET_NETWORK_ID}"`)) add("ledger-wording", `${p} renders a ledger value without the Devnet network check`);
   194	    const idx = h.match(/data-ledger-index="(\d+)"/);
   195	    if (!idx) add("ledger-wording", `${p} renders a ledger value without the ledger index`);
   196	    else indices.add(idx[1]);
   197	  }
   198	  if (indices.size > 1) add("ledger-wording", `pages name different ledgers: ${[...indices].join(", ")}`);
   199	  for (const [p, label] of [["static/observer/index.html", "Observer view: "], ["static/issuer/index.html", "Issuer&#x27;s copy: "]] as const) {
   200	    const n = (html.get(p) ?? "").split(label).length - 1;
   201	    if (html.has(p) && n !== DEMO_ACCOUNTS.length) add("accounts", `${p} renders ${n} account panels, not ${DEMO_ACCOUNTS.length}`);
   202	  }
   203	
   204	  // 9. The commit and the verdict, on every page.
   205	  for (const [p, h] of html) {
   206	    if (!h.includes(`/commit/${want.commit}`)) add("commit-and-verdict", `${p} does not name commit ${want.commit}`);
   207	    if (!h.includes("data-gate-verdict")) add("commit-and-verdict", `${p} has no gate-verdict slot`);
   208	  }
   209	
   210	  // 10. Licence notices for what is bundled, and nothing that should never be.
   211	  const lic = files.get("static/third-party-licenses.txt");
   212	  if (!lic) add("licences", "static/third-party-licenses.txt is missing");
   213	  else {
   214	    // Separator, `name@version (licence)`, separator, licence text: split on the
   215	    // separator lines, so each header is followed by its own body.
   216	    const parts = text(lic).split(/^={20,}$/m);
   217	    const names: [string, string, string][] = [];
   218	    for (let i = 1; i + 1 < parts.length; i += 2) {
   219	      const head = parts[i].trim().match(/^((?:@[^/\s]+\/)?[^@\s]+)@\S+ \([^)]*\)$/);
   220	      if (!head) { add("licences", `an entry header is malformed: ${JSON.stringify(parts[i].trim().slice(0, 60))}`); continue; }
   221	      names.push([head[0], head[1], parts[i + 1]]);
   222	    }
   223	    // Each notice must be the package's own licence file with only its email
   224	    // addresses removed (E-335), read from this checkout's node_modules at the
   225	    // same version. A version this checkout does not hold cannot be verified.
   226	    for (const [header, name, body] of names) {
   227	      const root = join(REPO, "node_modules", name);
   228	      const version = header.slice(name.length + 1, header.indexOf(" "));
   229	      const have = existsSync(join(root, "package.json")) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, "package.json"), "utf8")).version : null;
   230	      if (have !== version) { add("licences", `${name}@${version} cannot be verified: this checkout's node_modules holds ${have ?? "nothing"}`); continue; }

    41	export const HOSTED_ENDPOINT = "https://s.devnet.rippletest.net:51234";

    43	/** One account at the pinned ledger. Exported for tests. */
    44	export async function readAccount(
    45	  snap: { accountExists(a: string): Promise<boolean>; mptoken: (a: string, i: string) => Promise<any>; issuance: (i: string) => Promise<any>; index: number },
    46	  account: { address: string; issuanceId: string; label: string; note: string },
    47	  issuanceExists: boolean,
    48	): Promise<HostedAccount> {
    49	  const base = { address: account.address, label: account.label, note: account.note };
    50	  if (!(await snap.accountExists(account.address))) {
    51	    return { ...base, state: "account-missing", observer: null, issuerMirror: null };
    52	  }
    53	  if (!issuanceExists) return { ...base, state: "issuance-missing", observer: null, issuerMirror: null };
    54	  const mpt = await snap.mptoken(account.address, account.issuanceId);
    55	  if (!mpt) return { ...base, state: "no-position", observer: null, issuerMirror: null };
    56	  const observer = await observerView(snap as any, account.address, account.issuanceId);
    57	  return {
    58	    ...base,
    59	    state: "present",
    60	    observer,
    61	    issuerMirror: mpt.issuerEncryptedBalance
    62	      ? { present: true, ciphertext: mpt.issuerEncryptedBalance }
    63	      : { present: false },
    64	  };
    65	}
    66	
    67	export async function takeSnapshot(commit: string, canonicalUrl: string, endpoint = HOSTED_ENDPOINT): Promise<HostedSnapshot> {
    68	  if (endpoint !== HOSTED_ENDPOINT) throw new Error(`the hosted build reads ${HOSTED_ENDPOINT} and nothing else (ADR-0004 trigger 3)`);
    69	  if (!/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(commit)) throw new Error(`WCONF_HOSTED_COMMIT must be a full 40-hex commit id, not ${JSON.stringify(commit)}`);
    70	  if (!/^https:\/\/[a-z0-9.-]+\/?$/.test(canonicalUrl)) throw new Error(`WCONF_HOSTED_CANONICAL_URL must be an https origin, not ${JSON.stringify(canonicalUrl)}`);
    71	  const accounts = validDemoAccounts();
    72	  if (accounts.length !== DEMO_ACCOUNTS.length) throw new Error("a demo account failed its own format check; fix web/api/demo-accounts.ts");
    73	
    74	  const ledger = await LoopbackLedger.open(endpoint);
    75	  const snap = await ledger.snapshot();
    76	  const readAt = new Date().toISOString();
    77	
    78	  let issuanceExists = true;
    79	  let iss: any = null;
    80	  try {
    81	    iss = await snap.issuance(DEMO_ISSUANCE);
    82	  } catch (e) {
    83	    if (!(e instanceof LedgerRefusal && e.code === "REFUSED_LEDGER_ENTRY_MISSING")) throw e;
    84	    issuanceExists = false;
    85	  }
    86	
    87	  const out: HostedAccount[] = [];
    88	  for (const a of accounts) out.push(await readAccount(snap, a, issuanceExists));
    89	
    90	  return {
    91	    schema: SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA,
    92	    readAt,
    93	    commit,
    94	    canonicalUrl: canonicalUrl.replace(/\/$/, ""),
    95	    source: {
    96	      endpoint: ledger.endpoint,
    97	      networkId: ledger.identity.networkId,
    98	      buildVersion: ledger.identity.buildVersion,
    99	      ledgerIndex: snap.index,
   100	    },
   101	    issuance: issuanceExists
   102	      ? {
   103	          id: DEMO_ISSUANCE,
   104	          exists: true,
   105	          issuer: iss.issuer,
   106	          confidentialOutstandingAmount: iss.confidentialOutstandingAmountRaw,
   107	          issuerEncryptionKey: iss.issuerEncryptionKey,
   108	          hasAuditorKey: Boolean(iss.auditorEncryptionKey),
   109	        }
   110	      : { id: DEMO_ISSUANCE, exists: false },
   111	    accounts: out,
   112	    repositoryText: {
   113	      capabilities: {
   114	        rows: CAPABILITY_MATRIX,
   115	        invariants: INVARIANTS,
   116	        disclosures: { masterSeed: MASTER_SEED_DISCLOSURE, derivationNotPublished: DERIVATION_NOT_PUBLISHED },
   117	        namedGaps: { walletCodec: WALLET_CODEC_GAP },
   118	      },
   119	      custody: walkFlows(),
   120	    },
   121	  };
   122	}
   123	
   124	if (import.meta.main) {
   125	  const out = process.argv[2];
   126	  if (!out) throw new Error("usage: bun run web/hosted/snapshot.ts <out.json>");
   127	  const snapshot = await takeSnapshot(process.env.WCONF_HOSTED_COMMIT ?? "", process.env.WCONF_HOSTED_CANONICAL_URL ?? "");
   128	  writeFileSync(out, JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2) + "\n");
   129	  const states = snapshot.accounts.map((a) => `${a.label.split(" —")[0]}: ${a.state}`).join(", ");
   130	  console.log(`snapshot: ledger ${snapshot.source.ledgerIndex} on ${snapshot.source.endpoint}, rippled ${snapshot.source.buildVersion}; ${states}`);
   131	}
   265	  private cameFrom(what: string, r: any): void {
   266	    const index = r?.ledger_index;
   267	    if (r?.validated !== true || typeof index !== "number" || index !== this.index) {
   268	      throw new LedgerRefusal(
   269	        "REFUSED_LEDGER_TORN",
   270	        `${what} from ledger ${typeof index === "number" ? index : JSON.stringify(index ?? null)}` +
   271	          ` (validated: ${JSON.stringify(r?.validated ?? null)}), not the pinned, validated ${this.index}. ` +
   272	          `A snapshot assembled from two ledgers, or from one nobody validated, is a state that never existed`,
   273	      );
   274	    }
   275	  }
   276	
   277	  async sequenceOf(address: string): Promise<number> {
   278	    const r = await this.pinned("account_info", { account: address });
   279	    return Number(r.account_data.Sequence);
   280	  }
   281	
   282	  /**
   283	   * Whether `address` has an `AccountRoot` in the pinned ledger.
   284	   *
   285	   * Through `ledger_entry` rather than `account_info`, because a missing root
   286	   * answers `entryNotFound`, the one negative answer `pinned` checks for its
   287	   * ledger. Measured on Devnet with rippled 3.4.1 on 2026-10-20: a random
   288	   * address answered `entryNotFound` with `validated: true` and the pinned
   289	   * index. `ADR-0004` needs it so a Devnet reset renders as a missing account
   290	   * and not as an account holding nothing.
   291	   */
   292	  async accountExists(address: string): Promise<boolean> {
   293	    try {
   294	      entryOfType(await this.pinned("ledger_entry", { account_root: address }), "AccountRoot");
   295	      return true;
   296	    } catch (e) {
   297	      if (e instanceof LedgerRefusal && e.code === "REFUSED_LEDGER_ENTRY_MISSING") return false;
   298	      throw e;
   299	    }
   300	  }
   301	
   302	  /** Every field of one holder's position, or `null` if they hold no MPToken. */
   303	  async mptoken(address: string, issuanceId: string): Promise<MPTokenState | null> {
   304	    let r: any;
   305	    try {
   306	      r = await this.pinned("ledger_entry", {
   307	        mptoken: { mpt_issuance_id: issuanceId, account: address },
   308	      });
   309	    } catch (e) {
   310	      if (e instanceof LedgerRefusal && e.code === "REFUSED_LEDGER_ENTRY_MISSING") return null;
   311	      throw e;
   312	    }
   313	    const n = entryOfType(r, "MPToken");
   314	    return {
   315	      publicAmount: Number(n.MPTAmount ?? 0),
   316	      publicAmountRaw: String(n.MPTAmount ?? "0"),
   317	      holderEncryptionKey: n.HolderEncryptionKey,
   318	      confidentialBalanceSpending: n.ConfidentialBalanceSpending,
   319	      confidentialBalanceInbox: n.ConfidentialBalanceInbox,
   320	      confidentialBalanceVersion: Number(n.ConfidentialBalanceVersion ?? 0),
   321	      issuerEncryptedBalance: n.IssuerEncryptedBalance,
   322	      auditorEncryptedBalance: n.AuditorEncryptedBalance,
   323	    };
   324	  }
   325	
   326	  async issuance(issuanceId: string): Promise<IssuanceState> {
   327	    const r = await this.pinned("ledger_entry", { mpt_issuance: issuanceId });
   328	    const n = entryOfType(r, "MPTokenIssuance");
   329	    return {
   330	      issuer: n.Issuer,
   331	      // ⚠ **A JSON string, as rippled serialises every `UINT64`.** Reading it
   332	      // with a numeric helper sees every value as absent, and a preflight check
   333	      // that always passes looks identical to one that works. The signer has a
   334	      // control test for exactly this; so does `facility/tests`.
   335	      confidentialOutstandingAmount: Number(n.ConfidentialOutstandingAmount ?? 0),
   515	
   516	/**
   517	 * Refuse a non-loopback endpoint unless the risk has been accepted **by name**.
   518	 *
   519	 * ⚠ **Three refusals, not one.** An unset variable, a variable set to something
   520	 * else, and the accepted case are different situations and a caller who gets
   521	 * them confused is a caller who thinks they turned the hatch on. `REVIEW-013c`
   522	 * §3a B-VII is the standing reason: a refusal a client renders as "please try
   523	 * again" is a loud refusal made quiet.
   524	 */
   525	function assertRemoteRiskAccepted(endpoint: string): void {
   526	  const accepted = process.env.WCONF_ACCEPT_REMOTE_LEDGER_RISK;
   527	  if (accepted === RISK_ACCEPTANCE_PHRASE) {
   528	    // stderr, not stdout: a disclosure that can be lost to a pipe is a
   529	    // disclosure that will be.
   530	    process.stderr.write(`\n${REMOTE_LEDGER_DISCLOSURE}\n\n  endpoint: ${endpoint}\n\n`);
   531	    return;
   532	  }
   533	  if (accepted !== undefined) {
   534	    throw new LedgerRefusal(
   535	      "REFUSED_RISK_NOT_ACCEPTED",
   536	      `WCONF_ACCEPT_REMOTE_LEDGER_RISK is set, but not to the acceptance sentence. It must be ` +
   537	        `EXACTLY:\n\n    ${RISK_ACCEPTANCE_PHRASE}\n\n` +
   538	        `A near miss is refused rather than accepted, because a hatch that opens on anything ` +
   539	        `truthy is a hatch that opens by accident`,
   540	    );
   136	    inbox: classify(mpt?.confidentialBalanceInbox, encZero),
   137	    issuance: {
   138	      issuer: iss.issuer,
   139	      confidentialOutstandingAmount: iss.confidentialOutstandingAmountRaw,
   140	      hasIssuerKey: Boolean(iss.issuerEncryptionKey),
   141	      hasAuditorKey: Boolean(iss.auditorEncryptionKey),
   142	    },
   143	    whatIsPublic: WHAT_IS_PUBLIC,
   144	    whatIsHidden: WHAT_IS_HIDDEN,
   145	  };
   146	}
    30	          <div>
    31	            <h3 className="font-semibold mb-1">1. The derived key does not work with custodial key management</h3>
    32	            <p className="opacity-85 leading-relaxed">
    33	              The ElGamal secret is derived from the master seed, and a custody platform never releases
    34	              the seed. So a custodied account cannot derive its own ElGamal key or read its own
    35	              confidential balance.
    36	            </p>
    37	            <p className="opacity-85 leading-relaxed mt-2">
    38	              A standalone ElGamal key gets around this, but then something outside the custody
    39	              platform holds a permanent decryption key. Who that should be is an open question in
    40	              this project (CLAIMS.md E-117).
    41	            </p>
    42	          </div>
    43	          <div>
    44	            <h3 className="font-semibold mb-1">2. Approval policies cannot read a confidential amount</h3>
    45	            <p className="opacity-85 leading-relaxed">
    46	              An approval workflow sees a proof, not a value, so a rule like <em>&ldquo;two approvers
    47	              above $1M&rdquo;</em> has nothing to check. This is structural, not an integration
    48	              detail: confidentiality and amount-based approval policies pull against each other.
    49	            </p>
    50	          </div>
    51	        </div>
    52	      </Panel>
    53	
    54	      <Panel title="Which flows survive, and which break">
    55	        <p className="text-sm mb-2 opacity-80">
    56	          Each flow lists what it needs, and the verdict is computed from what a custody-shaped key
    57	          source has.
    58	        </p>
    59	        {notes.map((c, i) => (
    60	          <p key={c} className="text-sm mb-2 opacity-80">Note {i + 1}: {c}</p>
    61	        ))}
    61	
    62	/**
    63	 * ⚠ **Issue #10 is OPEN and no code discharges it.** The derivation is
    64	 * specified in one repository document and is not a published standard.
    65	 */
    66	/**
    67	 * ⚠ **A NAMED GAP, and it is deliberately NOT one of the reasons the wallet row
    68	 * says no.** `CLAIMS.md` E-206: whether a given wallet build's bundled codec can
    69	 * serialise the XLS-0096 types is **not determinable from any published
    70	 * source** — the page-side SDKs (`@crossmarkio/sdk@0.4.0`, `@gemwallet/api@3.8.0`,
    71	 * `xumm@1.8.0`) carry no codec dependency at all, so serialisation happens
    72	 * inside a closed extension bundle whose version nobody publishes.
    73	 *
    74	 * ⚠ **It is excluded from the reasoning on purpose.** It is a version fact an
    75	 * upstream release can close at any time; the three reasons the row DOES give
    76	 * are structural, so no codec release closes them, and only a wallet that held
    77	 * the viewing key and produced the proofs itself would (`CLAIMS.md` E-330).
    78	 * A demonstration resting
    79	 * on this one would be falsified by a release note.
    80	 */
    81	export const WALLET_CODEC_GAP =
    82	  "Not determined: whether a given wallet build can serialise XLS-0096 transactions. The " +
    83	  "page-side SDKs carry no codec, so serialisation happens inside the extension, whose version no " +
    84	  "vendor publishes. This is not why a wallet cannot hold a confidential position: the reasons " +
    85	  "above are structural, and this one could change with any release.";
    86	
    87	export const DERIVATION_NOT_PUBLISHED =
    88	  "The derivation is specified only in this repository and is not a published " +
    89	  "standard. A holder with their seed but without this repository cannot " +
    90	  "reconstruct their key. Issue #10 tracks this.";

codex
The reader succeeded against Devnet at validated ledger `6269733`. In a local inconsistent-response test, though, the actual `Snapshot` reader accepted an MPToken as present on one read and missing on the next. `readAccount()` returned `state: "present"` with public amount `"0"`, `registered: false`, and the issuer mirror from the first answer. It also accepts conflicting ledger hashes when the index matches. Neither case is covered by the passing snapshot tests.

    23	export async function compareDeployed(root: string, origin: string): Promise<string[]> {
    24	  const base = join(root, ".vercel", "output");
    25	  const verdict = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(base, "static/gate-verdict.json"), "utf8"));
    26	  const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(base, "config.json"), "utf8"));
    27	  const want: Record<string, string> = config.routes[0].headers;
    28	  const problems: string[] = [];
    29	  const get = async (path: string) => {
    30	    const r = await fetch(origin.replace(/\/$/, "") + path, { redirect: "manual", headers: { "cache-control": "no-cache" } });
    31	    if (r.headers.get("set-cookie")) problems.push(`${path}: the host set a cookie`);
    32	    return r;
    33	  };
    34	  const checkHeaders = (path: string, r: Response) => {
    35	    for (const h of CHECKED_HEADERS) if (r.headers.get(h) !== want[h]) problems.push(`${path}: ${h} is ${JSON.stringify(r.headers.get(h))}, not what config.json sets`);
    36	  };
    37	  for (const [p, digest] of Object.entries<string>(verdict.perFile)) {
    38	    if (!p.startsWith("static/")) continue;
    39	    const path = p.slice("static".length);
    40	    const r = await get(path);
    41	    if (r.status !== 200) { problems.push(`${path}: HTTP ${r.status}`); continue; }
    42	    if (sha256(await r.arrayBuffer()) !== digest) problems.push(`${path}: the served bytes differ from what the gate passed`);
    43	    checkHeaders(path, r);
    44	  }
    45	  for (const page of HOSTED_PAGES) {
    46	    const path = `/${page}`;
    47	    const r = await get(path);
    48	    const file = page ? `static/${page}/index.html` : "static/index.html";
    49	    if (r.status !== 200) { problems.push(`${path}: HTTP ${r.status}`); continue; }
    50	    if (sha256(await r.arrayBuffer()) !== verdict.perFile[file]) problems.push(`${path}: the page served at its route differs from ${file}`);
    51	    checkHeaders(path, r);
    52	  }
    53	  const served = await get("/gate-verdict.json");
    54	  if (sha256(await served.arrayBuffer()) !== sha256(readFileSync(join(base, "static/gate-verdict.json")))) problems.push("/gate-verdict.json differs from the local one");
    55	  const missing = await get(`/no-such-page-${Date.now()}`);
    56	  if (missing.status !== 404) problems.push(`an unknown path answered ${missing.status}, not 404`);
    57	  return problems;
    58	}
    59	
    60	if (import.meta.main) {
    61	  const [root, origin] = process.argv.slice(2);
    30	  return status === "identical" || status === "ahead";
    31	}
    32	
    33	export function preflight(root: string, isOnPublicMain: (commit: string) => boolean = onPublicMain): string[] {
    34	  const problems: string[] = [];
    35	  const manifestPath = join(root, "build-manifest.json");
    36	  if (!existsSync(manifestPath)) return [`no build-manifest.json beside the output; build with web/hosted/build.ts`];
    37	  const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifestPath, "utf8"));
    38	  if (manifest.trial) problems.push("the manifest says TRIAL: this output was built from a working tree, not a commit");
    39	  else if (!isOnPublicMain(manifest.commit)) problems.push(`${manifest.commit} is not on the public repository's main, so the footer's link names a commit readers cannot see`);
    40	  const files = readOutput(root);
    41	  const v = files.get("static/gate-verdict.json");
    42	  if (!v) return [...problems, "no static/gate-verdict.json: the gate has not passed this output"];
    43	  const verdict = JSON.parse(v.toString("utf8"));
    44	  if (verdict.verdict !== "PASS") problems.push(`the verdict is ${JSON.stringify(verdict.verdict)}`);
    45	  if (verdict.commit !== manifest.commit) problems.push(`the gate checked ${verdict.commit}, the build was of ${manifest.commit}`);
    46	  const entries = [...files].filter(([p]) => p !== "static/gate-verdict.json").sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b));
    47	  if (entries.length !== verdict.files) problems.push(`${entries.length} files now, ${verdict.files} when the gate passed`);
    48	  for (const [p, b] of entries) if (verdict.perFile[p] !== sha256(b)) problems.push(`${p} changed since the gate passed`);
    49	  const digest = sha256(entries.map(([p, b]) => `${p}\t${sha256(b)}`).join("\n"));
    50	  if (digest !== verdict.outputDigest) problems.push("the output digest does not match the verdict's");
    51	  return problems;
    52	}
    53	
    54	if (import.meta.main) {
    55	  const root = process.argv[2];
    22	## Finding 1 — the ruled key derivation is incompatible with custodial key management
    23	
    24	**The chain, each link in this repository:**
    25	
    26	1. A confidential operation requires the **ElGamal secret** — to decrypt the balance being spent and to produce the proof — in addition to the XRPL account key that signs.
    27	2. Under the ruled key generation (`docs/reviews/REVIEW-012-RULING-keygen-2026-08-18.md`, implemented in `signer/src/keygen.rs`), the ElGamal secret is **derived from the account's master family seed**.
    28	3. A custody platform's entire purpose is **never to release seed material**. Releasing it would defeat the custody.
    29	
    30	**Therefore a custodied account cannot derive its own viewing key.** It cannot read its own confidential balance, which is not a limitation of any integration — it follows from step 2 alone.
    31	
    32	⚠ **The escape hatch exists and it moves the problem rather than solving it.** `KeySource::Standalone` (`signer/src/onboarding.rs:279`) is an independent ElGamal secret with its own backup, and it is what every profile written before 2026-08-20 silently was. But then **something outside the custody boundary holds a permanent decryption credential for every balance the account has ever held** — and *who holds it* is `CLAIMS.md` **E-117**, which is open and has had no adversarial review.
    33	
    34	⚠ **E-117's axis is the honest framing, and it is sharper than a custody question:** *confidential positions, or non-custodial pooling — one or the other, today.* This project picks confidentiality because that is its premise. A design that needs *"no single party can move the float"* weighs it the other way, and ~~the comparison table in `ADR-0002` **has no row for custody at all**~~ **(struck 2026-09-13, `CLAIMS.md` E-295: the row has existed since 2026-08-20, and the same clause was struck at `:86` one round earlier without reaching this copy)**.
    35	
    36	**What would change this:** a derivation whose input is not the master seed, or a custody platform that performs the derivation inside its own boundary and never emits either secret. **The second is not obviously impossible** — it is a key-derivation function over a seed the platform already holds — and it is the question worth putting to a custody vendor. ⚠ **It would require the derivation to be a published standard, which is issue #10, open, and no code discharges it.**
    37

   305	export function runControls(root: string, want: Expect): { run: number; failed: string[] } {
   306	  const failed: string[] = [];
   307	  let run = 0;
   308	  const fresh = () => { const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "check-web-hosted-")); cpSync(join(root, ".vercel"), join(d, ".vercel"), { recursive: true }); return d; };
   309	  const dirs: string[] = [];
   310	  try {
   311	    const clean = fresh(); dirs.push(clean);
   312	    run++;
   313	    const base = runChecks(readOutput(clean), want);
   314	    if (base.length) failed.push(`the unbroken copy must pass, and has ${base.length} finding(s): ${base[0].check}: ${base[0].detail}`);
   315	    for (const [name, check, mutate] of CONTROLS) {
   316	      const d = fresh(); dirs.push(d);
   317	      run++;
   318	      mutate(d);
   319	      const got = runChecks(readOutput(d), want);
   320	      if (!got.some((x) => x.check === check)) failed.push(`${name}: expected a '${check}' finding, got ${got.length ? got.map((x) => x.check).join(", ") : "none"}`);
   321	    }
   322	    // The secret scan, through the same function the real check calls.
    42	  const headers: Record<string, string> = config.routes[0].headers;
    43	  const rewrites: [RegExp, string][] = config.routes.filter((r: any) => r.dest).map((r: any) => [new RegExp(r.src), r.dest]);
    44	  return Bun.serve({
    45	    hostname: "127.0.0.1",
    46	    port: 0,
    47	    fetch(req) {
    48	      let path = new URL(req.url).pathname;
    49	      for (const [re, dest] of rewrites) if (re.test(path)) { path = dest; break; }
    50	      if (path === "/") path = "/index.html";
    51	      const file = join(base, "static", path);
    52	      if (!file.startsWith(join(base, "static")) || !existsSync(file) || !statSync(file).isFile()) return new Response("not found", { status: 404, headers });
    53	      const ext = file.slice(file.lastIndexOf(".") + 1);
    54	      return new Response(Bun.file(file), { headers: { ...headers, "Content-Type": TYPES[ext] ?? "application/octet-stream" } });
    55	    },
    56	  });
    57	}

/**
 * observer-harness.ts — exactly what a full-ledger observer can see.
 *
 * CLAUDE.md requires this: *"a demo of the happy path is not evidence of
 * confidentiality"*. This is the counterpart to `issuer-decrypt-balance.ts` —
 * that one shows what the issuer sees, this one shows what everybody sees.
 *
 *   bun run tools/observer-harness.ts <account> <MPTokenIssuanceID>
 *   bun run tools/observer-harness.ts <account> <id> --assert-encrypted-zero
 *
 * ## It holds no keys, and it links no XLS-96 cryptography
 *
 * That is the point. An observer has neither. It uses general-purpose primitives
 * — `@noble/hashes` for SHA-256 and `@noble/curves` for secp256k1 — and nothing
 * from mpt-crypto: no vendored C library, no WASM module, no secret. The
 * canonical `EncZero` is recomputed from three PUBLIC inputs: the holder's
 * registered encryption key, the AccountID and the MPTokenIssuanceID.
 *
 * *(An earlier version of this comment said "links no cryptography library",
 * which was false — it links two. REVIEW-006 caught it.)*
 *
 * ## Its second test is randomness reuse
 *
 * `--assert-no-r-reuse` scans the account's confidential transactions and fails
 * if the ElGamal encryption randomness `r` was ever reused. It needs no key:
 * `C1 = r*G` is on the wire, so reuse is visible to anyone, and when it happens
 * the DIFFERENCE between two hidden amounts falls out by subtraction and a
 * bounded discrete log. Executed against deliberately-broken transactions on
 * Devnet — see `CLAIMS.md` E-63 and `tools/spike-randomness-2026-08-18/`.
 *
 * This is a self-check as much as an audit: our own signer could regress into
 * it, and nothing on the ledger would complain. rippled accepts reused `r`.
 *
 * ## Its first test is F-1
 *
 * `CLAIMS.md` F-1 says the reset/initialised balance value is the canonical
 * `EncZero`, recomputable by anyone, so such a balance is **publicly known to be
 * exactly zero** — contradicting documentation that called it indistinguishable.
 * `--assert-encrypted-zero` exits non-zero unless that is demonstrated on live
 * ledger state, which is what "a test that fails if the claim is false" means
 * here.
 *
 * ## What this tool is NOT allowed to imply
 *
 * Read `CLAIMS.md` P-4, P-9 and P-11 before changing any output string. Amounts
 * are hidden. Identities, timing, counterparties and transaction frequency are
 * not, and the issuer can always decrypt. The report says so out loud on every
 * run because a confidentiality demo that omits it is the failure mode this
 * repository exists to avoid.
 */
import { secp256k1 } from "@noble/curves/secp256k1";
import { sha256 } from "@noble/hashes/sha256";
import { decodeAccountID, encodeAccountID } from "ripple-address-codec";

const DEVNET_WS = "wss://s.devnet.rippletest.net:51233";
const DEVNET_NETWORK_ID = 2;

/**
/**
 * wconf-keygen.ts — the ruled ElGamal derivation, for TypeScript callers.
 *
 * # Why this file exists
 *
 * `REVIEW-012-RULING-keygen-2026-08-18.md` §2 rules how a holder's ElGamal
 * secret is derived from their XRPL master seed, and
 * `docs/reviews/REVIEW-012c` adjudicated it. The construction lives in that
 * ruling and **only** there; this is an *implementation* of its prose, and
 * where the two disagree **the ruling wins**.
 *
 * Before 2026-08-25 there were two byte-identical copies of it in `tools/` —
 * one in `spike-step6-2026-08-20/devnet-derived-key.ts`, one in
 * `spike-step7-2026-08-24/devnet-convert-back.ts` — and architecture §6 step 7
 * was about to add a third. `REVIEW-005c`'s lesson is that a second copy of a
 * construction is a divergence waiting to happen; a third is that lesson
 * ignored twice. This is the single copy those callers now import.
 *
 * # ⚠ What the independence that matters actually is
 *
 * The cross-check that makes the Devnet drivers evidence is **TypeScript
 * against Rust**, mediated by a validated ledger entry: `signer/src/keygen.rs`
 * derives the key the account registers, and a driver derives it again here
 * and compares. Collapsing three identical TypeScript copies into one does not
 * weaken that, because they never differed. What it removes is three places
 * for a future edit to land in two of.
 *
 * ⚠ `tools/spike-keygen-2026-08-18/t-keygen-construction.ts` stays the KAT and
 * stays independent — it runs the construction through **two** library paths
 * (raw HMAC and @noble's `hkdf`) precisely so the vectors are reproducible from
 * the prose rather than from one code path. **A KAT that imported the thing it
 * tests would be worthless**, so it does not import this and this does not
 * import it.
 *
 * # The self-check, and why it is not decoration
 *
 * Like `wconf-randomness.ts`, this **reproduces the ruling's published vectors
 * before it will derive anything** — including the `PRK` and `OKM`
 * intermediates, so a divergence is located rather than merely detected. A
 * caller that gets a key from this module has already been told the module
 * agrees with §6 of the ruling.
 *
 * # ⚠ The reduction is TOTAL and has NO abort path
 *
 * Unlike the sigma-nonce and `r`/`ρ` rulings, which both say *abort on zero,
 * never retry*. That is correct there, where the input is fresh entropy and an
 * abort costs one transaction. **Keygen's input is a fixed seed**, so an abort
 * would be permanent — that holder could never participate. `(OKM mod (n−1)) +
 * 1` cannot yield zero and cannot yield `n`. Do not "fix" it back.
 *
 * # ⚠ What deriving buys, and what it does not
 *
 * A derived key is reconstructible from the master seed **under this
 * derivation**, which is the only thing deriving buys. It is not "recoverable"
 * in any wider sense: XLS-0096 has no rotation and no recovery (`CLAIMS.md`
 * P-10), and the derivation is **not a published standard** (issue #10), so a
 * holder who has their seed and not this repository cannot reconstruct their
 * key. Those are two sentences about two layers and merging them is
 * `CLAIMS.md` E-125 and E-126.
 *
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const STYLE: Record<string, string> = {
  yes: "bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-900 dark:bg-emerald-950 dark:text-emerald-200",
  no: "bg-red-100 text-red-900 dark:bg-red-950 dark:text-red-200",
  conditional: "bg-amber-100 text-amber-900 dark:bg-amber-950 dark:text-amber-200",
  unverified: "bg-slate-200 text-slate-800 dark:bg-slate-800 dark:text-slate-200",
};

const LABEL: Record<string, string> = {
  yes: "yes",
  no: "no",
  conditional: "conditional",
  unverified: "⚠ unverified",
};

export function Verdict({ v }: { v: string }) {
  return (
    <span className={`inline-block rounded px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold ${STYLE[v] ?? STYLE.unverified}`}>
      {LABEL[v] ?? v}
    </span>
  );
}

export function Panel({ title, tone = "plain", children }: { title: string; tone?: "plain" | "warn"; children: ReactNode }) {
  const border = tone === "warn" ? "border-[var(--color-warn)]" : "border-black/10 dark:border-white/15";
  return (
    <section className={`border ${border} rounded-lg p-5 mb-6`}>
      <h2 className="font-semibold mb-3">{title}</h2>
      {children}
    </section>
  );
}
